subproblems.title: Covering a countably n-rectifiable set by Lipschitz pieces with continuous injective derivative (replaces Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and the C¹ approximation step)
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 0, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, and let M ⊆ E be countably n-rectifiable in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.1 (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n M: M ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M_0) = 0 and F_j: ℝⁿ → E Lipschitz, ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)). Then there are a Borel set N_0 ⊆ E with Hⁿ(N_0) = 0, compact sets C_i ⊆ ℝⁿ and Lipschitz maps F_i: ℝⁿ → E (i ∈ ℕ) such that M ⊆ N_0 ∪ ⋃_i F_i(C_i) and, for every i: F_i is differentiable at every w ∈ C_i with injective derivative DF_i(w); w ↦ DF_i(w) is continuous on C_i; and there is c_i > 0 with c_i|v − w| ≤ |F_i(v) − F_i(w)| for all v, w ∈ C_i.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (M : Set (Ambient n ℓ)), 0 < n → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n M → ∃ (N₀ : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (C : ℕ → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (F : ℕ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Ambient n ℓ), MeasurableSet N₀ ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) N₀ = 0 ∧ M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃ i, F i '' C i ∧ ∀ i, IsCompact (C i) ∧ (∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K (F i)) ∧ (∀ w ∈ C i, DifferentiableAt ℝ (F i) w ∧ Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ (F i) w)) ∧ ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ (F i)) (C i) ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ v ∈ C i, ∀ w ∈ C i, c * ‖v - w‖ ≤ ‖F i v - F i w‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. n ≥ 1 and ℓ ≥ 0 are integers; ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ (volume) and Euclidean norm |·|; E := Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}; Hⁿ := μHE[n] (on E, and on ℝⁿ, where Hⁿ = Lⁿ by Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); B_r(q) is the closed ball; a linear map L: ℝⁿ → E is injective iff min_{|e|=1}|Le| > 0. Lip(F) denotes a Lipschitz constant of F. M is countably n-rectifiable (Simon Ch. 3, 1.1; Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n M): M ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_{j∈ℕ} F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M_0) = 0 and every F_j: ℝⁿ → E Lipschitz.

Source and role. Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 ('only if') covers M, up to an Hⁿ-null set, by countably many embedded C¹ submanifolds, using the C¹ Approximation Theorem (Ch. 2, Thm 1.5), whose printed proof rests on Whitney's extension theorem (Ch. 2, Thm 1.6, quoted there without proof). Neither theorem is available as an axiom-checked declaration in the pinned references: GMT/Ch02/Contract.lean states C1Approximation and WhitneyExtension only as unproved conjuncts of the Chapter 2 contract, and SimonGMT's Chapter02/WhitneyExtension.lean is not part of the built library. The printed proofs of Ch. 3, 1.6 '⇒', 1.8(1), 1.9 and of the area formula 2.4 use the submanifolds only through countably many injective parametrizations whose derivative is injective and continuous on the parameter set. This lemma provides exactly such a covering, by Lipschitz pieces with continuous injective derivative on compact parameter sets, directly from Rademacher's theorem, the Lipschitz area formula and Lusin's theorem. All results used are pinned, axiom-checked declarations (standard axioms only):
(L1) Rademacher (Simon Ch. 2, 1.4): a Lipschitz map ℝⁿ → E is differentiable Lⁿ-a.e. [Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt; SimonGMT Chapter02.rademacher_ae_differentiableAt].
(L2) Lipschitz images (Simon Ch. 2, 1.8(i)): Hⁿ(F(A)) ≤ Lip(F)ⁿ Hⁿ(A) for every A ⊆ ℝⁿ [SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn].
(L3) Regular set and the null image of its complement (area formula, Simon Ch. 2, §3): for Lipschitz F: ℝⁿ → E the set R_F := {w : F is differentiable at w and DF(w) is injective} (SimonGMT Chapter02.areaRegularSet F) is Borel [Chapter02.measurableSet_areaRegularSet], and Hⁿ(F(S ∖ R_F)) = 0 for every S ⊆ ℝⁿ [Chapter02.area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero].
(L4) w ↦ DF(w) is Borel measurable [Mathlib measurable_fderiv].
(L5) Lusin (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17): if ν is a Borel measure on ℝⁿ that is inner regular by closed sets on Borel sets of finite measure, A is Borel with ν(A) < ∞ and g: ℝⁿ → ℝ is Borel, then for each δ > 0 there is a closed C ⊆ A with ν(A ∖ C) < δ and g continuous on C [SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable]. Lⁿ is weakly regular, so it is inner regular by closed sets on Borel sets of finite measure [Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt], and also by compact sets.
(L6) Every Hⁿ-null set is contained in a Borel Hⁿ-null set [Mathlib MeasureTheory.exists_measurable_superset_of_null].

Step 1 (regular points lie in Borel sets of uniform local injectivity). Fix a Lipschitz map F: ℝⁿ → E. For an integer k ≥ 1 let
S_k := R_F ∩ ⋂_{u ∈ ℝⁿ, |u| ≤ 1/k} {w ∈ ℝⁿ : |F(w + u) − F(w)| ≥ |u|/k}.
For fixed u the set {w : |F(w + u) − F(w)| ≥ |u|/k} is closed because F is continuous, so the intersection over u is closed, and S_k (a closed set intersected with the Borel set R_F) is Borel. We claim R_F = ⋃_{k≥1} S_k. The inclusion ⊇ is clear. Let w ∈ R_F. Since DF(w) is injective and the unit sphere of ℝⁿ is compact and nonempty (n ≥ 1), m := min_{|e|=1}|DF(w)e| > 0, so |DF(w)u| ≥ m|u| for all u ∈ ℝⁿ. By differentiability of F at w there is r > 0 with |F(w + u) − F(w) − DF(w)u| ≤ (m/2)|u| whenever |u| ≤ r; then |F(w + u) − F(w)| ≥ |DF(w)u| − (m/2)|u| ≥ (m/2)|u| for |u| ≤ r. Choose an integer k ≥ max(2/m, 1/r). For |u| ≤ 1/k we have |u| ≤ r, hence |F(w + u) − F(w)| ≥ (m/2)|u| ≥ |u|/k; so w ∈ S_k.

Step 2 (injectivity with a lower Lipschitz bound). Fix k ≥ 1 and an enumeration (q_m)_{m∈ℕ} of the points of ℝⁿ with rational coordinates. The closed balls Q_{k,m} := B_{1/(2k)}(q_m), m ∈ ℕ, cover ℝⁿ (these points are dense). If v, w ∈ S_k ∩ Q_{k,m}, then |v − w| ≤ 1/k, and the defining property of S_k at the point w, applied with u := v − w, gives
(2.1) |F(v) − F(w)| ≥ |v − w|/k for all v, w ∈ S_k ∩ Q_{k,m}.

Step 3 (compact pieces on which DF is continuous; Lusin). Fix k, m and put S := S_k ∩ Q_{k,m}, a bounded Borel set, so Lⁿ(S) < ∞. Fix j ≥ 1. Choose orthonormal bases (e_a) of ℝⁿ and (e'_b) of E; the N := n(n + ℓ) matrix entries g_{ab}(w) := ⟨DF(w)e_a, e'_b⟩ are real Borel functions by (L4) (evaluation at e_a and the inner product with e'_b are continuous). For each (a, b), (L5) applied to ν := Lⁿ, A := S and g := g_{ab} gives a closed D_{ab} ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S ∖ D_{ab}) < 1/(2Nj) on which g_{ab} is continuous; inner regularity of Lⁿ gives a compact K' ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S ∖ K') < 1/(2j). Put C_{k,m,j} := K' ∩ ⋂_{a,b} D_{ab}. Then C_{k,m,j} is compact, C_{k,m,j} ⊆ S, Lⁿ(S ∖ C_{k,m,j}) < 1/(2j) + N/(2Nj) = 1/j, and every entry of DF is continuous on C_{k,m,j}; since DF(w) = Σ_{a,b} g_{ab}(w)·E_{ab} with the fixed linear maps E_{ab} := ⟨e_a, ·⟩e'_b, w ↦ DF(w) is continuous on C_{k,m,j}. The set Z_{k,m} := S ∖ ⋃_{j≥1} C_{k,m,j} satisfies Lⁿ(Z_{k,m}) ≤ Lⁿ(S ∖ C_{k,m,j}) < 1/j for every j, hence Lⁿ(Z_{k,m}) = 0.

Step 4 (properties of each piece). Let C := C_{k,m,j}. Then: C is compact; C ⊆ S_k ⊆ R_F, so F is differentiable at every w ∈ C and DF(w) is injective; w ↦ DF(w) is continuous on C (Step 3); and, as C ⊆ S_k ∩ Q_{k,m}, (2.1) gives (1/k)|v − w| ≤ |F(v) − F(w)| for all v, w ∈ C, so the constant c := 1/k > 0 works.

Step 5 (the remainder has null image). By Steps 1 and 2, ℝⁿ = (ℝⁿ ∖ R_F) ∪ ⋃_{k≥1, m∈ℕ} (S_k ∩ Q_{k,m}), and by Step 3, S_k ∩ Q_{k,m} ⊆ Z_{k,m} ∪ ⋃_{j≥1} C_{k,m,j}. Hence F(ℝⁿ) ⊆ F(ℝⁿ ∖ R_F) ∪ F(Z_F) ∪ ⋃_{k,m,j} F(C_{k,m,j}) with Z_F := ⋃_{k,m} Z_{k,m}, a countable union of Lⁿ-null sets. By (L3), Hⁿ(F(ℝⁿ ∖ R_F)) = 0; by (L2) and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ(F(Z_F)) ≤ Lip(F)ⁿ Lⁿ(Z_F) = 0. So Y_F := F(ℝⁿ ∖ R_F) ∪ F(Z_F) is Hⁿ-null and F(ℝⁿ) ⊆ Y_F ∪ ⋃_{k,m,j} F(C_{k,m,j}).

Step 6 (all parametrizations; conclusion). Write M ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_{j∈ℕ} F_j(ℝⁿ) as in 1.1 and apply Steps 1–5 to every F_j, obtaining compact pieces C^{(j)}_{k,m,p} (k ≥ 1, m ∈ ℕ, p ≥ 1) with the properties of Step 4 for the map F_j (constant 1/k), and Hⁿ-null sets Y_{F_j}. The set of all quadruples (j, k, m, p) is countable; fix a bijection from ℕ onto it, i ↦ (j(i), k(i), m(i), p(i)), and put F_i := F_{j(i)} (Lipschitz) and C_i := C^{(j(i))}_{k(i),m(i),p(i)}. Then
M ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_j Y_{F_j} ∪ ⋃_{i∈ℕ} F_i(C_i),
and N_0' := M_0 ∪ ⋃_j Y_{F_j} is Hⁿ-null as a countable union of null sets. By (L6) there is a Borel set N_0 ⊇ N_0' with Hⁿ(N_0) = 0, and M ⊆ N_0 ∪ ⋃_i F_i(C_i). For every i, C_i is compact, F_i is Lipschitz, F_i is differentiable at every w ∈ C_i with injective derivative, w ↦ DF_i(w) is continuous on C_i, and c_i := 1/k(i) > 0 satisfies c_i|v − w| ≤ |F_i(v) − F_i(w)| for all v, w ∈ C_i (Step 4). This is the assertion.
proof_key_steps: Rademacher and the area formula: the image of the non-regular set ℝⁿ ∖ R_F (DF missing or not injective) is Hⁿ-null
R_F = ⋃_k S_k with S_k Borel, where |F(w+u) − F(w)| ≥ |u|/k for |u| ≤ 1/k
On S_k ∩ B_{1/(2k)}(q), F is injective with |F(v) − F(w)| ≥ |v − w|/k
Lusin (entrywise) and inner regularity give compact C ⊆ S_k ∩ B_{1/(2k)}(q) with DF|_C continuous, exhausting it up to an Lⁿ-null set whose image is Hⁿ-null
Enumerate the pieces of all parametrizations and absorb the null images into a Borel Hⁿ-null N_0

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes a.e., the tangent-field interface (GF), and the first variation formula
subproblems.statement: (1) ApproxTangentAE: for all n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 0 and every admissible pair a = (M, θ) in ℝ^{n+ℓ}, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M: exactly one subspace P satisfies (mk a).IsApproxTangentAt x P; the chosen tangent space (mk a).tangentSpace x is the approximate tangent space of M with respect to θ at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.7 (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt); and μ_V(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρⁿ) → θ(x) as ρ ↓ 0. (2) (GF): for all n ≥ 1, ℓ and every rectifiable n-varifold V in ℝ^{n+ℓ}, μ_V is finite on compact sets, dim T_xV = n for μ_V-a.e. x, and x ↦ p_{T_xV} is μ_V-a.e. strongly measurable. (3) FirstVariationFormula: for every pair a, every n ≥ 1 and every compact variation (φ, ε, K) as in Ch. 4, 2.1, the function t ↦ (imageMass a (φ t) K).toReal = M(φ_t#(V⌞K)) has derivative ∫ div_M X dμ_V at t = 0, where X(y) = ∂_tφ(t, y)|_{t=0}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ApproxTangentAE ∧ (∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ), 0 < n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts V.weight ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, Module.finrank ℝ (V.tangentSpace x) = n) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection) V.weight) ∧ FirstVariationFormula
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions (used throughout). n ≥ 1 and ℓ ≥ 0 are integers, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, Hⁿ = μHE[n] (equal to Simon's Hⁿ), B_ρ(ξ) = closedBall ξ ρ (closed ball), ω_n = omega n ∈ (0, ∞), and Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ for every n-dimensional subspace P. For a rectifiable n-varifold V: μ = μ_V = V.weight; T_x = V.tangentSpace x; p_x and p_x^⊥ are the orthogonal projections onto T_x and T_x^⊥; div_M X(x) = V.tangentialDiv X x = trace(DX(x)∘p_x); ∇^M h(x) = V.tangentialGradient h x = p_x(∇h(x)); r = |x − ξ|; q_ξ(x) = V.normalRadialSq ξ x = |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|² ∈ [0, 1] (q_ξ(ξ) = 0 because division by 0 is 0); w_ξ(x) = q_ξ(x)/|x − ξ|ⁿ (w_ξ(ξ) = 0); a_ξ(ρ) = μ(B_ρ(ξ))/ρⁿ (a real number); Θ(ξ) = V.density ξ. A test field in U is a C¹ map X: E → E with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U (IsTestField). 'V has mean curvature H in U' (HasMeanCurvatureIn) means H ∈ L¹_loc(U, μ) and ∫div_M X dμ = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every test field X in U; 'stationary in U' means ∫div_M X dμ = 0 for every test field X in U. (FV) for V means: (FV1) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K; (FV2) dim T_x = n for μ-a.e. x; (FV3) x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. (GF) is the statement that (FV) holds for every n ≥ 1, every ℓ and every V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ (exactly the second conjunct of the sibling tangent_structure_first_variation); (AT) is the contract Prop ApproxTangentAE. Under (FV): q_ξ, w_ξ, ∇^M h (for h ∈ C¹(U), on U) and div_M X (for X ∈ C¹) are μ-a.e. strongly measurable, being continuous functions of p_x and of continuous data; |div_M X| ≤ (n+ℓ)‖DX‖ and div_M X = 0 off tsupport X, so div_M X is μ-integrable for every test field X; μ is a locally finite, hence outer regular, Borel measure, and μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0 (spt V = spt μ).

Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.3, Theorem 1.6 ('⇒') with Remark 1.5(2), Remark 1.8(1)(2), Theorem 1.9 ('⇒'), the area formula of Ch. 3 §2 (2.4–2.5, from Ch. 2 §3 and 4.11–4.13); Ch. 4, 1.3 and 2.2 (with the computation of Ch. 2 §5, 5.2–5.3). The printed proofs use the covering of Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 by embedded C¹ submanifolds N_j only through injective parametrizations with continuous injective derivative; here these are the Lipschitz pieces F_i(C_i) supplied by the sibling theorem rectifiable_lipschitz_piece_cover (which replaces Lemma 1.2 and its use of the C¹ Approximation Theorem). The printed arguments are otherwise reproduced in order, with the details required by the contract's formulation (closed balls, the weight μ_V, the chosen tangent space). No errata apply to these items.

Additional notation. For a pair a = (M, θ) write V = mk a and μ = μ_V = pairWeight n M θ, so ∫g dμ = ∫_M gθ dHⁿ for Borel g ≥ 0 and μ(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dHⁿ for Borel A. Every V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ equals mk a for some pair a (it is a quotient). ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ (= Hⁿ on ℝⁿ). η_{x,λ}(y) := λ^{-1}(y − x); p_P is the orthogonal projection onto a subspace P. For an injective linear A: ℝⁿ → E, JA := (det(A*A))^{1/2} > 0; for a Lipschitz G: ℝⁿ → E, JG(v) := J(DG(v)) at points where G is differentiable (this is SimonGMT Chapter02.areaJacobianAt G v = (fderiv ℝ G v).normDet). For a linear Λ: E → E and a subspace T with inclusion ι_T, J^TΛ := (Λ restricted to T).normDet = (det(ι_T*Λ*Λι_T))^{1/2} = (det(p_TΛ*Λp_T + I − p_T))^{1/2}, a continuous function of (Λ, p_T) (for T = {0} it equals 1).

Results used as known theorems (all pinned and axiom-checked, standard axioms only).
(R1) The sibling theorem rectifiable_lipschitz_piece_cover.
(R2) Area formula for Lipschitz maps (Simon Ch. 2, §3): if G: ℝⁿ → E is Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝⁿ is Borel and G is injective on B, then ∫_{G(B)} u dHⁿ = ∫_B JG(v) u(G(v)) dv for every u: E → [0, ∞] [SimonGMT Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn]; and Hⁿ(G(A)) ≤ Lip(G)ⁿ Lⁿ(A) for every A ⊆ ℝⁿ [Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn with Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume]. For an injective linear A: ℝⁿ → E the area formula reads ∫_{A(ℝⁿ)} u dHⁿ = JA∫_{ℝⁿ} u(Av) dv; in particular Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ for every n-dimensional subspace P.
(R3) Upper density theorem (Simon Ch. 1, Thm 3.6) [SimonGMT Chapter01.ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside, applied to the outer measure of ν, which is Borel regular by Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular, together with Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure; the density there is normalised by the constant realUnitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞), which does not affect vanishing]: if ν is a Borel measure on E and A ⊆ E is Borel with ν(A) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ A, limsup_{ρ↓0} ν(A ∩ B_ρ(x))/ρⁿ = 0.
(R4) Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17) [SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable], for finite Borel measures on E (these are weakly regular, so inner regular by closed sets on Borel sets — Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt — and, E being proper, by compact sets), and Lebesgue's density theorem [Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div]: for every C ⊆ ℝⁿ, Lⁿ(C ∩ B_r(w))/Lⁿ(B_r(w)) → 1 as r ↓ 0 for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ C.
(R5) Two regular, locally finite Borel measures on E with the same integrals of all functions in C_c(E) are equal [Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported]; for an n-dimensional subspace P, Hⁿ⌞P is regular [SimonGMT Chapter03.regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule] (hence so is cHⁿ⌞P, c > 0) and supp(Hⁿ⌞P) = P [Chapter03.support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule].
(R6) Hⁿ(cA + b) = cⁿHⁿ(A) for c > 0 and b ∈ E (Hⁿ is translation invariant and homogeneous of degree n under dilations); every Hⁿ-null set lies in a Borel Hⁿ-null set; an Hⁿ-null-measurable set contains a Borel set and is contained in a Borel set, both differing from it by Hⁿ-null sets.

Part A. Approximate tangent planes and the tangent field.

1. (Pieces, in place of Lemma 1.2.) Fix a pair a = (M, θ). M is countably n-rectifiable (IsRectifiablePair), so (R1) gives a Borel set N_0 with Hⁿ(N_0) = 0, compact sets C_i ⊆ ℝⁿ and Lipschitz maps F_i: ℝⁿ → E (indexed by i ≥ 1 after shifting the index) with M ⊆ N_0 ∪ ⋃_{i≥1} N_i, N_i := F_i(C_i), such that for every i: F_i is differentiable at each w ∈ C_i with DF_i(w) injective, w ↦ DF_i(w) is continuous on C_i, and c_i|v − w| ≤ |F_i(v) − F_i(w)| for all v, w ∈ C_i, with c_i > 0. Consequences: N_i is compact (a continuous image of a compact set); F_i maps C_i bijectively onto N_i, and the inverse ψ_i: N_i → C_i is (1/c_i)-Lipschitz, hence continuous; for x ∈ N_i, T_i(x) := DF_i(ψ_i(x))(ℝⁿ) is an n-dimensional subspace; x ↦ p_{T_i(x)} is continuous on N_i, being the composition of ψ_i, of DF_i restricted to C_i, and of the map A ↦ p_{A(ℝⁿ)} = A(A*A)^{-1}A*, which is continuous on injective linear maps A: ℝⁿ → E; Hⁿ(N_i) ≤ Lip(F_i)ⁿLⁿ(C_i) < ∞ by (R2); and JF_i is continuous, hence bounded by some constant Γ_i, on the compact set C_i (DF_i is continuous on C_i and A ↦ JA is continuous).

2. (Remark 1.3.) Put M_0' := M ∩ N_0 and M_i := (M ∩ N_i) ∖ (N_0 ∪ ⋃_{1≤j<i} N_j) (i ≥ 1). These sets are Hⁿ-null-measurable (M is, and the N_j are Borel), pairwise disjoint, cover M (a point of M ∖ N_0 lies in M_i for the least i with x ∈ N_i), Hⁿ(M_0') = 0, and M_i ⊆ N_i ∖ ⋃_{1≤j<i} N_j.

3. (Blow-up of a piece at a density point.) Let i ≥ 1, let w ∈ C_i be a Lebesgue density point of C_i (so λ^{-n}Lⁿ(B_{λr}(w) ∖ C_i) → 0 as λ ↓ 0, for every r > 0), x := F_i(w), A := DF_i(w) and T := T_i(x) = A(ℝⁿ). Then
(3a) λ^{-n}∫_{N_i} f(η_{x,λ}(y)) dHⁿ(y) → ∫_T f dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0, for every f ∈ C_c(E);
(3b) λ^{-n}Hⁿ(N_i ∩ B_{Rλ}(x)) ≤ Lip(F_i)ⁿω_n(R/c_i)ⁿ for all λ, R > 0.
Proof of (3b): N_i ∩ B_{Rλ}(x) = F_i(C_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(B_{Rλ}(x))), and C_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(B_{Rλ}(x)) ⊆ B_{Rλ/c_i}(w) by the lower bound of step 1; apply (R2).
Proof of (3a): let spt f ⊆ B_R(0), m_A := min_{|e|=1}|Ae| > 0 and R' := R/min(c_i, m_A). By (R2) for F_i on the Borel set C_i (applied to the positive and negative parts of f∘η_{x,λ}; all integrals are finite because Hⁿ(N_i) < ∞ and JF_i ≤ Γ_i on C_i) and the substitution v = w + λu,
λ^{-n}∫_{N_i} f(η_{x,λ}) dHⁿ = λ^{-n}∫_{C_i} f((F_i(v) − x)/λ) JF_i(v) dv = ∫_{ℝⁿ} 1_{C_i}(w + λu) f(Q_λ(u)) JF_i(w + λu) du, where Q_λ(u) := (F_i(w + λu) − F_i(w))/λ.
If w + λu ∈ C_i and |u| > R', then |Q_λ(u)| ≥ c_i|u| > R, so the integrand vanishes; and |Au| ≥ m_A|u| > R for |u| > R', so f(Au) = 0 there. By (R2) for A, ∫_T f dHⁿ = JA∫_{ℝⁿ} f(Au) du = ∫_{B_{R'}(0)} f(Au) JF_i(w) du (JA = JF_i(w)). Therefore the difference D_λ of the two sides of (3a) satisfies
|D_λ| ≤ ∫_{B_{R'}(0)} 1_{C_i}(w + λu)|f(Q_λ(u))JF_i(w + λu) − f(Au)JF_i(w)| du + sup|f|·JF_i(w)·λ^{-n}Lⁿ(B_{λR'}(w) ∖ C_i).
The second term tends to 0 because w is a density point of C_i. In the first term, for |u| ≤ R' with w + λu ∈ C_i we have |Q_λ(u) − Au| ≤ R'·sup_{0<|h|≤λR'}|F_i(w + h) − F_i(w) − Ah|/|h| → 0 (differentiability of F_i at w) and |JF_i(w + λu) − JF_i(w)| ≤ sup{|JF_i(v) − JF_i(w)| : v ∈ C_i, |v − w| ≤ λR'} → 0 (continuity of DF_i on C_i at w and of A' ↦ JA'); since f is bounded and uniformly continuous and JF_i ≤ Γ_i on C_i, the integrand tends to 0 uniformly on B_{R'}(0) (it is at most ω_f(|Q_λ(u) − Au|)Γ_i + sup|f|·|JF_i(w + λu) − JF_i(w)|, ω_f a modulus of continuity of f). Hence D_λ → 0.

4. (Theorem 1.9 via the proof of 1.6 '⇒' and Remark 1.8(1).) Claim: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is i ≥ 1 with x ∈ M_i such that, with P_x := T_i(x),
(★) λ^{-n}∫ f(η_{x,λ}(y)) dμ(y) = λ^{-n}∫_M f(η_{x,λ}(y))θ(y) dHⁿ(y) → θ(x)∫_{P_x} f dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0, for every f ∈ C_c(E).
Proof. As Hⁿ(M_0') = 0, it suffices to fix i ≥ 1 and prove (★) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_i. (i) The set Z_i of points of C_i that are not Lebesgue density points of C_i is Lⁿ-null (R4), so F_i(Z_i) is Hⁿ-null (R2); every x ∈ N_i ∖ F_i(Z_i) equals F_i(w) for the density point w = ψ_i(x). (ii) θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M (M = ⋃_k M ∩ B_k(0) and θ is integrable on each M ∩ B_k(0)), so there is a Borel function θ̃ with θ = θ̃ Hⁿ-a.e. on M (Mathlib AEMeasurable.mk), and by (R6) a Borel Hⁿ-null set Y with θ = θ̃ on M ∖ Y. For q ≥ 1, by (R6) choose a Borel set A_q ⊆ M_i ∩ {θ̃ ≥ 1/q} ∩ B_q(0) ∖ Y differing from this null-measurable set by an Hⁿ-null set; Hⁿ(A_q) ≤ q∫_{M∩B_q(0)} θ dHⁿ < ∞. By (R4) applied to the finite Borel measure Hⁿ⌞A_q and the Borel function θ̃ (and inner regularity by compact sets), for each m ≥ 1 there is a compact C_{q,m} ⊆ A_q with Hⁿ(A_q ∖ C_{q,m}) < 1/m on which θ = θ̃ is continuous. Since θ > 0 on M, M_i ∖ Y ⊆ ⋃_q (M_i ∩ {θ̃ ≥ 1/q} ∩ B_q(0) ∖ Y); hence the countably many compact sets C_{q,m} cover M_i up to an Hⁿ-null set, and it suffices to prove (★) for Hⁿ-a.e. x in one of them, C. Note C ⊆ M_i ⊆ N_i. (iii) Choose r_C > 0 with C ⊆ ball 0 r_C. Apply (R3) to ν := μ (a Borel measure, finite on balls since μ(B) = ∫_{M∩B} θ dHⁿ) with A := B_{r_C}(0) ∖ C, and to ν := Hⁿ⌞N_i (finite) with A := N_i ∖ C: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C and every R > 0, (a) λ^{-n}μ(B_{Rλ}(x) ∖ C) → 0 and (b) λ^{-n}Hⁿ((N_i ∖ C) ∩ B_{Rλ}(x)) → 0 as λ ↓ 0 (for small λ, B_{Rλ}(x) ⊆ ball 0 r_C). Fix such an x with x ∉ F_i(Z_i), and f ∈ C_c(E) with spt f ⊆ B_R(0), so that f(η_{x,λ}(y)) = 0 unless |y − x| ≤ Rλ. Since C ⊆ M ∩ N_i, λ^{-n}∫_M f(η_{x,λ})θ dHⁿ = I_1 + I_2 + I_3 + I_4 with I_1 := θ(x)λ^{-n}∫_{N_i} f(η_{x,λ}) dHⁿ, I_2 := −θ(x)λ^{-n}∫_{N_i∖C} f(η_{x,λ}) dHⁿ, I_3 := λ^{-n}∫_C f(η_{x,λ}(y))(θ(y) − θ(x)) dHⁿ(y) and I_4 := λ^{-n}∫_{M∖C} f(η_{x,λ})θ dHⁿ (all integrals finite). By (3a), I_1 → θ(x)∫_{T_i(x)} f dHⁿ; |I_2| ≤ θ(x) sup|f| λ^{-n}Hⁿ((N_i ∖ C) ∩ B_{Rλ}(x)) → 0 by (b); |I_3| ≤ sup|f|·sup_{y∈C∩B_{Rλ}(x)}|θ(y) − θ(x)|·λ^{-n}Hⁿ(N_i ∩ B_{Rλ}(x)) → 0 by continuity of θ on C and (3b); |I_4| ≤ sup|f| λ^{-n}μ(B_{Rλ}(x) ∖ C) → 0 by (a). This proves (★) with P_x = T_i(x).

5. (ApproxTangentAE.) Let x be as in step 4; then x ∈ M and θ(x) > 0. (i) dim P_x = n and (★) is V.IsApproxTangentAt x P_x with c = θ(x) > 0. (ii) If also V.IsApproxTangentAt x Q with a constant c' > 0 (so dim Q = n), then c'∫_Q f dHⁿ = θ(x)∫_{P_x} f dHⁿ for all f ∈ C_c(E) (uniqueness of limits), so the regular locally finite measures c'Hⁿ⌞Q and θ(x)Hⁿ⌞P_x are equal by (R5). Evaluating both on B_1(0) gives c'ω_n = θ(x)ω_n (R2), so c' = θ(x) > 0 and Hⁿ⌞Q = Hⁿ⌞P_x; taking supports (R5), Q = P_x. Hence there is exactly one such P, and the chosen V.tangentSpace x equals P_x. (iii) For r > 0, η_{x,r} is a similarity of ratio r^{-1}, so by (R6) ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) = r^{-n}∫_M f(η_{x,r}(z))θ(z) dHⁿ(z) → θ(x)∫_{P_x} f dHⁿ by (★); together with dim P_x = n this is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x (V.tangentSpace x). (iv) (Ch. 3, 1.8(2), with closed balls.) For δ ∈ (0, 1) take f_± ∈ C_c(E) with 0 ≤ f_± ≤ 1, f_+ = 1 on B_1(0), spt f_+ ⊆ B_{1+δ}(0), f_− = 1 on B_{1−δ}(0), spt f_− ⊆ ball 0 1. Then ∫ f_−(η_{x,λ}) dμ ≤ μ(B_λ(x)) ≤ ∫ f_+(η_{x,λ}) dμ, and (★) with Hⁿ(P_x ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ (R2) gives θ(x)ω_n(1 − δ)ⁿ ≤ liminf_{λ↓0} λ^{-n}μ(B_λ(x)) ≤ limsup_{λ↓0} λ^{-n}μ(B_λ(x)) ≤ θ(x)ω_n(1 + δ)ⁿ. Letting δ ↓ 0, μ(B_λ(x))/(ω_nλⁿ) → θ(x), i.e. V.HasDensityAt x (θ x). Since this holds for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and for every pair, ApproxTangentAE holds.

6. (GF.) Let V = mk a. (i) For compact K, μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (local integrability of θ), so IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ. (ii) μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M (a measure with density), and by step 5 dim V.tangentSpace x = n for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, hence for μ-a.e. x. (iii) Define g: E → (E →L E) by g(x) := p_{T_i(x)} for x ∈ N_i ∖ ⋃_{1≤j<i} N_j (i ≥ 1) and g(x) := 0 elsewhere. The sets N_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} N_j are Borel and pairwise disjoint and g is continuous on each of them (step 1), so g is Borel measurable, hence strongly measurable (finite-dimensional codomain). For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M we have x ∈ M_i ⊆ N_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} N_j for some i and V.tangentSpace x = T_i(x) (steps 4, 5), i.e. p_x = g(x); since μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M this holds μ-a.e., so x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. This proves (GF).

Part B. The first variation formula (Ch. 4, 2.2).

7. Let a = (M, θ), V = mk a, μ = μ_V, n ≥ 1, and (φ, ε, K) with IsCompactVariation φ ε K; put φ_t := φ t and X(y) := deriv (t ↦ φ t y) 0 = ∂_tφ(t, y)|_{t=0}. As φ is C^∞ on the open set (−ε, ε) × E, X is C^∞ and (t, y) ↦ Dφ_t(y) is C^∞ with ∂_t Dφ_t(y)|_{t=0} = DX(y) (symmetry of second derivatives). For y ∉ K we have φ_t(y) = y for all t, so X = 0 on the open set E ∖ K, DX = 0 there and div_M X = 0 off K. For |t| < ε, φ_t is a bijection with C^∞ inverse, so Function.invFun φ_t = φ_t^{-1}, Dφ_t(y) is invertible for every y (chain rule for φ_t^{-1}∘φ_t = id), and φ_t is a homeomorphism; Dφ_t is continuous and equals the identity on the open set E ∖ K (where φ_t = id), so it is bounded and φ_t is globally Lipschitz; hence φ_t maps Borel sets to Borel sets and Hⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets.

8. (Area formula on M; Ch. 3, 2.4–2.5.) For |t| < ε and every x ∈ E let J_t(x) := J^{T_x}(Dφ_t(x)) = (det(p_xDφ_t(x)*Dφ_t(x)p_x + I − p_x))^{1/2}, with T_x = V.tangentSpace x and p_x its projection (where no tangent exists T_x = ⊥ and J_t(x) = 1); x ↦ J_t(x) is μ-a.e. equal to the Borel function obtained by replacing p_x with g(x) (step 6). Claim: imageMass a φ_t K = ∫⁻_{φ_t(M∩K)} ofReal(θ(φ_t^{-1}(y))) dHⁿ(y) = ∫⁻_{M∩K} ofReal(θ J_t) dHⁿ. Proof: M ∩ K is the disjoint union of M_0' ∩ K and the sets M_i ∩ K (step 2); φ_t is injective, so their images are pairwise disjoint and Hⁿ-null-measurable, and Hⁿ(φ_t(M_0' ∩ K)) = 0. Fix i ≥ 1. Choose a Borel set A with M_i ∩ K ⊆ A ⊆ N_i and Hⁿ(A ∖ (M_i ∩ K)) = 0 (R6; intersect a Borel hull with the Borel set N_i), and let B := C_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(A), a Borel set with F_i(B) = A on which F_i and the Lipschitz map φ_t∘F_i are injective. For v ∈ B, F_i is differentiable at v and φ_t is C^∞, so D(φ_t∘F_i)(v) = Dφ_t(F_i(v))DF_i(v). For linear A': ℝⁿ → E and Λ: E → E, J(ΛA') = J^{A'(ℝⁿ)}(Λ)·J(A') [Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_comp; SimonGMT Chapter02.areaJacobian_comp_eq_parametrization_mul_tangential] (for injective A' = ιA_0, with ι the inclusion of A'(ℝⁿ) and A_0 invertible: det(A'^*Λ^*ΛA') = det(ι^*Λ^*Λι)·det(A_0^*A_0)). Hence J(φ_t∘F_i)(v) = J^{T_i(F_i(v))}(Dφ_t(F_i(v)))·JF_i(v) for v ∈ B. For every u: E → [0, ∞], (R2) applied to φ_t∘F_i on B and then to F_i on B gives
∫⁻_{φ_t(A)} u dHⁿ = ∫⁻_B J^{T_i(F_i(v))}(Dφ_t(F_i(v)))·u(φ_t(F_i(v)))·JF_i(v) dv = ∫⁻_A J^{T_i(x)}(Dφ_t(x))·u(φ_t(x)) dHⁿ(x).
Take u := ofReal(θ∘φ_t^{-1}), so that u(φ_t(x)) = ofReal(θ(x)). Since A ∖ (M_i ∩ K) and its image under φ_t are Hⁿ-null, and T_i(x) = T_x for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_i (steps 4, 5), ∫⁻_{φ_t(M_i∩K)} ofReal(θ∘φ_t^{-1}) dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{M_i∩K} ofReal(θ J_t) dHⁿ. Summing over i proves the claim.

9. (Ch. 2 §5.) Fix x with P := T_x of dimension n, let ι: P → E be the inclusion and Gram_t := (Dφ_t(x)ι)*(Dφ_t(x)ι), so J_t(x) = (det Gram_t)^{1/2}, Gram_0 = I_P, and d/dt Gram_t at t = 0 equals (DX(x)ι)*ι + ι*(DX(x)ι), whose trace is 2 trace(ι*DX(x)ι) = 2 trace(DX(x)∘p_P) = 2 div_M X(x). By Jacobi's formula at the identity (det(I + tB + o(t)) = 1 + t·trace B + o(t), from the Leibniz expansion of the determinant), the derivative of det Gram_t at t = 0 is trace(d/dt Gram_t at 0), hence d/dt J_t(x) at t = 0 equals div_M X(x). Uniform bound: on the compact set [−ε/2, ε/2] × K the maps (t, y) ↦ Dφ_t(y), ∂_tDφ_t(y) and Dφ_t(y)^{-1} are continuous, hence bounded in operator norm by some Λ_1 ≥ 1. Fix x ∈ K and an n-plane P. For |t| ≤ ε/2, t ↦ Gram_t is C¹, ‖Gram_t‖ ≤ Λ_1², Gram_t ≥ Λ_1^{-2}I_P (because |Dφ_t(x)v| ≥ Λ_1^{-1}|v|), so Gram_t is invertible with ‖Gram_t^{-1}‖ ≤ Λ_1², and ‖∂_tGram_t‖ ≤ 2Λ_1². Writing det(Gram_t + H) = det Gram_t·det(I + Gram_t^{-1}H) and applying Jacobi's formula at the identity, d/dt det Gram_t = det Gram_t·trace(Gram_t^{-1}∂_tGram_t); as det Gram_t > 0, t ↦ J_t(x) = (det Gram_t)^{1/2} is differentiable on [−ε/2, ε/2] with ∂_tJ_t(x) = ½J_t(x)·trace(Gram_t^{-1}∂_tGram_t). Since J_t(x) ≤ ‖Dφ_t(x)‖ⁿ ≤ Λ_1ⁿ and |trace Y| ≤ n‖Y‖, |∂_tJ_t(x)| ≤ ½Λ_1ⁿ·n·Λ_1²·2Λ_1² = nΛ_1^{n+4} =: C_1 for all |t| ≤ ε/2, all x ∈ K and every n-plane P (at t = 0 the formula reduces to the value div_M X(x) found above). Where T_x = ⊥, J_t(x) = 1 for all t. Moreover x ↦ J_t(x) is μ-measurable, being a continuous function of Dφ_t(x) and of p_x, which equals the Borel g(x) μ-a.e. (step 6).

10. (Conclusion.) Let m(t) := ∫_{M∩K} θ J_t dHⁿ for |t| ≤ ε/2; J_0 = 1, so m(0) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ. By step 9 and the mean value theorem, |θ(x)(J_t(x) − J_0(x))/t| ≤ C_1θ(x) with θ ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K)), and the quotient tends to θ(x) div_M X(x) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ K (namely wherever dim T_x = n, by step 9). By dominated convergence m is differentiable at 0 with m'(0) = ∫_{M∩K} θ div_M X dHⁿ = ∫_K div_M X dμ = ∫ div_M X dμ (step 7). Since m(t) ≤ (1 + C_1ε)∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞, step 8 gives imageMass a φ_t K = ofReal(m(t)) and (imageMass a (φ t) K).toReal = m(t) for |t| ≤ ε/2. Hence t ↦ (imageMass a (φ t) K).toReal has derivative ∫ V.tangentialDiv X dμ_V at t = 0, which is FirstVariationFormula. With steps 5 and 6 the conjunction is proved.

subproblems.statement: Assume (GF) (for every n ≥ 1, ℓ and every rectifiable n-varifold V: μ_V is finite on compacts, dim T_xV = n μ_V-a.e., and x ↦ p_{T_xV} is μ_V-a.e. strongly measurable) and FirstVariationFormula. Conventions (used throughout). n ≥ 1 and ℓ ≥ 0 are integers, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, Hⁿ = μHE[n] (equal to Simon's Hⁿ), B_ρ(ξ) = closedBall ξ ρ (closed ball), ω_n = omega n ∈ (0, ∞), and Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ for every n-dimensional subspace P. A test field in U is a C¹ map X: E → E with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U (IsTestField). 'V has mean curvature H in U' (HasMeanCurvatureIn) means H ∈ L¹_loc(U, μ) and ∫div_M X dμ = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every test field X in U; 'stationary in U' means ∫div_M X dμ = 0 for every test field X in U. (FV) for V means: (FV1) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K; (FV2) dim T_x = n for μ-a.e. x; (FV3) x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. (GF) is the statement that (FV) holds for every n ≥ 1, every ℓ and every V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ (exactly the second conjunct of the sibling tangent_structure_first_variation); (AT) is the contract Prop ApproxTangentAE. The printed one-line argument is made precise: a C^∞ compactly supported field is realized as the initial velocity of the variation φ_t(x) = x + tX(x), and C¹ fields are reached by mollification, using (GF) to pass to the limit in the integrals.

Hypotheses: (GF) and FirstVariationFormula (FVF). Fix n ≥ 1, ℓ, a pair a = (M, θ), V = mk a, μ = μ_V, and an open set U. For a variation φ write X_φ(y) := deriv (t ↦ φ t y) 0.

1. (⇒) Assume V is stationary in U and let (φ, ε, K) satisfy IsCompactVariation φ ε K with K ⊆ U. Since φ is C^∞ on the open set (−ε, ε) × E, X_φ is C^∞, in particular C¹. For y ∉ K, φ t y = y for all t ∈ (−ε, ε), so X_φ(y) = 0; hence the support of X_φ lies in K, tsupport X_φ ⊆ K (K is compact, hence closed) ⊆ U, and X_φ has compact support. Put L := sup_y ‖DX(y)‖ < ∞, ε := 1/(L + 1), φ(t, y) := y + tX(y) and K := tsupport X (compact). We check IsCompactVariation φ ε K: ε > 0; K is compact; (t, y) ↦ y + tX(y) is C^∞; for |t| < ε the map φ_t is injective because |φ_t(y) − φ_t(y')| ≥ (1 − |t|L)|y − y'|, and surjective because for z ∈ E the map y ↦ z − tX(y) is a contraction with constant |t|L < 1 whose fixed point y satisfies φ_t(y) = z; Dφ_t(y) = I + tDX(y) is invertible since ‖tDX(y)‖ < 1, so by the inverse function theorem the inverse of the bijection φ_t is C^∞, and Function.invFun φ_t is this inverse; φ(0, y) = y; for y ∉ K, X(y) = 0 and φ(t, y) = y. Since K_0 is compact and U is open there is δ > 0 with K_1 := {y : dist(y, K_0) ≤ δ} ⊆ U (any δ > 0 if U = E); K_1 is compact. Let η_k ≥ 0 be C^∞ mollifiers with ∫ η_k = 1 and spt η_k ⊆ B_{1/k}(0), and X_k := η_k * X (componentwise convolution). 1. g is differentiable at every point. For x ≠ ξ, r is differentiable with Dr(x)v = ⟨(x − ξ)/r, v⟩, so Dg(x)v = γ(r)v + γ'(r)⟨(x − ξ)/r, v⟩(x − ξ). At ξ: g(ξ + v) − γ(0)v = (γ(|v|) − γ(0))v and |γ(|v|) − γ(0)| ≤ (sup_{[0,1]}|γ'|)|v| for |v| ≤ 1, so g(ξ + v) = γ(0)v + o(|v|) and Dg(ξ) = γ(0)I.

2. For x ∈ U, h is differentiable at x (U is open and h ∈ C¹(U)), hence X = hg is differentiable at x with DX(x)v = (Dh(x)v)g(x) + h(x)Dg(x)v.

3. Trace identity: if T is an n-dimensional subspace with orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_n and p = p_T, then trace(A∘p) = Σ_i ⟨Aτ_i, τ_i⟩ for every linear A: E → E (compute the trace in an orthonormal basis of E extending (τ_i); p kills the added vectors).

5. X ≡ 0 on the open set E ∖ tsupport X, so DX = 0 and div_M X = 0 there; as tsupport X ⊆ U, div_M X = 0 on E ∖ U and ∫ div_M X dμ = ∫_U div_M X dμ. By step 4 and (FV2), div_M X = Φ μ-a.e. on U, so ∫_U div_M X dμ = ∫_U Φ dμ (Bochner integrals of a.e.-equal functions are equal).

6. X = 0 off U and ⟨X(x), H(x)⟩ = h(x)γ(r)⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩, so ∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ = ∫_U hγ(r)⟨x − ξ, H⟩ dμ.

K_1 is compact. On the open set E ∖ tsupport h, h ≡ 0, hence h = 0 and ∇h = 0 there. Consequently there is A_0 with |h| ≤ A_0 and |∇h| ≤ A_0 on B_{(1+ε_0)ρ} (continuity on the compact K_1 ⊆ U, zero elsewhere in the ball), H is μ-integrable on K_1 (H ∈ L¹_loc(U, μ)), and h, ∇^M h, hH, G vanish on B_{(1+ε_0)ρ} ∖ K_1.

Step 1 (measurability; the two integrability conclusions). By (FV3) and continuity of ∇h on U, ∇^M h and q are μ-a.e. strongly measurable on B_{(1+ε_0)ρ}. By Step 0, |G| ≤ (1 + ε_0)ρA_0(1 + |H|)1_{K_1} on B_{(1+ε_0)ρ}, so G is μ-integrable there ((FV1): μ(K_1) < ∞). The function L is bounded by ‖G 1_{K_1}‖_{L¹(μ)} on (0, ρ] and Borel, since L(τ) = ∫_{B_τ} G⁺ dμ − ∫_{B_τ} G⁻ dμ is a difference of two nondecreasing functions of τ; so τ ↦ L(τ)/τ^{n+1} is bounded by σ^{-n-1}‖G 1_{K_1}‖_{L¹(μ)} on (σ, ρ] and integrable there. On B_ρ ∖ B_σ we have r > σ, so |h w| ≤ A_0σ^{-n}; h w is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and μ(B_ρ) < ∞, so h w is μ-integrable on B_ρ ∖ B_σ.

Step 2 (cutoff and test fields). Fix ε ∈ (0, ε_0/2] and a C^∞ nonincreasing φ = φ_ε: ℝ → [0, 1] with φ = 1 on (−∞, 1] and φ = 0 on [1 + ε, ∞) (so −2/ε ≤ φ' ≤ 0 may be arranged; only boundedness of φ' is used). Let Ω := (σ/2, (1 + ε_0)ρ/(1 + ε)), an open interval containing [σ, ρ]. For τ ∈ Ω let γ_τ(t) := φ(t/τ), a C¹ function with γ_τ'(t) = φ'(t/τ)/τ, and X_τ(x) := h(x)γ_τ(r)(x − ξ). Since (1 + ε)τ < (1 + ε_0)ρ, tsupport h ∩ B_{(1+ε)τ} ⊆ K_1 ⊆ U. X_τ is a test field in U: it is C¹ on U (product of C¹ functions; x ↦ γ_τ(r)(x − ξ) is C^∞ because γ_τ is constant near 0), it vanishes on the open set W_τ := E ∖ (tsupport h ∩ B_{(1+ε)τ}) (there h = 0 or γ_τ(r) = 0), U ∪ W_τ = E, so X_τ is C¹ on E; and tsupport X_τ ⊆ tsupport h ∩ B_{(1+ε)τ}, a compact subset of U.

Step 3 (first variation; 3.3 and 5.1). By the sibling theorem radial_first_variation (hypothesis (FV2)) applied to X_τ:
∫_U [h(nφ(r/τ) + (r/τ)φ'(r/τ)(1 − q)) + φ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h⟩] dμ = −∫_U hφ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, H⟩ dμ.
All integrands vanish outside K_1 ⊆ U (Step 0, and φ(r/τ) = φ'(r/τ) = 0 for r ≥ (1 + ε)τ), and they are μ-integrable (bounded by a constant times (1 + |H|)1_{K_1}). So the integrals may be taken over E and split. With I(τ) := ∫ hφ(r/τ) dμ, J(τ) := ∫ hφ(r/τ) q dμ and L_ε(τ) := ∫ φ(r/τ) G dμ this reads
(3.1) n I(τ) + ∫ h (r/τ)φ'(r/τ) dμ − ∫ h (r/τ)φ'(r/τ) q dμ + L_ε(τ) = 0 (τ ∈ Ω).
Since ∂_τ[φ(r/τ)] = −(r/τ²)φ'(r/τ) is continuous in τ and bounded by sup|φ'|(1 + ε_0)ρ/τ² uniformly in x, differentiation under the integral sign (dominating function a constant times |h|1_{K_1}) shows that I and J are C¹ on Ω with τI'(τ) = −∫ h (r/τ)φ'(r/τ) dμ and τJ'(τ) = −∫ h (r/τ)φ'(r/τ) q dμ. Thus (3.1) becomes n I(τ) − τI'(τ) + τJ'(τ) + L_ε(τ) = 0.

Step 4 (3.4). Hence (τ^{-n}I(τ))' = τ^{-n-1}(τI'(τ) − nI(τ)) = τ^{-n}J'(τ) + τ^{-n-1}L_ε(τ) on Ω, and integrating over [σ, ρ] (fundamental theorem of calculus for the C¹ function τ^{-n}I):
(4.1) ρ^{-n}I_ε(ρ) − σ^{-n}I_ε(σ) = ∫_σ^ρ τ^{-n}J_ε'(τ) dτ + ∫_σ^ρ τ^{-n-1}L_ε(τ) dτ.
By Fubini (the integrand (τ, x) ↦ τ^{-n}h(x)q(x)(r/τ²)(−φ'(r/τ)) is bounded on [σ, ρ] × K_1 and vanishes for x ∉ K_1), ∫_σ^ρ τ^{-n}J_ε'(τ) dτ = ∫ h(x)q(x)k_ε(r(x)) dμ(x), where k_ε(s) := ∫_σ^ρ τ^{-n}∂_τ[φ(s/τ)] dτ.

Step 5 (the kernel k_ε; corrected 3.5). For s > 0, ∂_τ[φ(s/τ)] = −(s/τ²)φ'(s/τ) ≥ 0 vanishes unless 1 ≤ s/τ ≤ 1 + ε, i.e. s/(1 + ε) ≤ τ ≤ s, where s^{-n} ≤ τ^{-n} ≤ (1 + ε)ⁿs^{-n}. Since ∫_σ^ρ ∂_τ[φ(s/τ)] dτ = φ(s/ρ) − φ(s/σ) ≥ 0,
s^{-n}(φ(s/ρ) − φ(s/σ)) ≤ k_ε(s) ≤ (1 + ε)ⁿ s^{-n}(φ(s/ρ) − φ(s/σ)).
In particular k_ε(s) = 0 for s ≤ σ (both values of φ equal 1), 0 ≤ k_ε ≤ 2ⁿσ^{-n}, and since φ_ε(t) → 1 for t ≤ 1 and φ_ε(t) → 0 for t > 1 as ε ↓ 0, k_ε(s) → s^{-n}1_{σ<s≤ρ} for every s ≥ 0 (k_ε(0) = 0).

Step 6 (ε ↓ 0). Let ε = ε_m ↓ 0 with ε_m ≤ ε_0/2. By dominated convergence (dominating functions A_0 1_{K_1}, 2ⁿσ^{-n}A_0 1_{K_1}, |G| 1_{K_1}, all μ-integrable): I_ε(τ) → ∫_{B_τ} h dμ for each τ ∈ [σ, ρ] (φ_ε(r/τ) → 1_{B_τ}); ∫ h q k_ε(r) dμ → ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} h q r^{-n} dμ = ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} h w dμ; L_ε(τ) → L(τ) for each τ with |L_ε(τ)| ≤ ‖G 1_{K_1}‖_{L¹(μ)}, so by dominated convergence on [σ, ρ], ∫_σ^ρ τ^{-n-1}L_ε(τ) dτ → ∫_{(σ,ρ]} τ^{-n-1}L(τ) dτ. Passing to the limit in (4.1):
ρ^{-n}∫_{B_ρ} h dμ − σ^{-n}∫_{B_σ} h dμ = ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} h q_ξ |x − ξ|^{-n} dμ + ∫_{(σ,ρ]} τ^{-n-1}∫_{B_τ}⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h + hH⟩ dμ dτ,
which, with Step 1, is the asserted conjunction.
proof_key_steps: Compactness gives ε_0 > 0 with tsupport h ∩ B_{(1+ε_0)ρ}(ξ) ⊆ U; h, ∇h bounded there and zero off tsupport h; H integrable there
Measurability from (FV3); boundedness gives the two integrability conclusions
X_τ = hφ_ε(r/τ)(x−ξ) is a test field; radial_first_variation gives nI − τI' + τJ' + L_ε = 0 (3.3/5.1)
(τ^{-n}I)' = τ^{-n}J' + τ^{-n-1}L_ε; integrate over [σ, ρ] and use Fubini for the J' term (3.4)
Kernel bounds s^{-n}(φ(s/ρ)−φ(s/σ)) ≤ k_ε(s) ≤ (1+ε)ⁿ s^{-n}(φ(s/ρ)−φ(s/σ)) (corrected 3.5)
Let ε ↓ 0 by dominated convergence to obtain the identity with closed balls

subproblems.title: Stationary monotonicity identity, existence and upper semicontinuity of the density (Simon 3.6–3.11)
subproblems.statement: Assume (GF). Then StationaryMonotonicity holds (for V stationary in open U and B_R(ξ) ⊆ U: ρ^{-n}μ_V(B_ρ) − σ^{-n}μ_V(B_σ) = ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} q_ξ|x − ξ|^{-n}dμ_V for 0 < σ ≤ ρ < R; ρ ↦ ρ^{-n}μ_V(B_ρ) is nondecreasing on (0, R); and for 0 < ρ < R the integrand is μ_V-integrable on B_ρ with (ω_nρⁿ)^{-1}μ_V(B_ρ) − Θⁿ(μ_V, ξ) = ω_n^{-1}∫_{B_ρ} q_ξ|x − ξ|^{-n}dμ_V), and StationaryDensity holds (Θⁿ(μ_V, ·) exists at every point of U and is upper semicontinuous on U).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ), 0 < n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts V.weight ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, Module.finrank ℝ (V.tangentSpace x) = n) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection) V.weight) → StationaryMonotonicity ∧ StationaryDensity
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions (used throughout). n ≥ 1 and ℓ ≥ 0 are integers, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, Hⁿ = μHE[n] (equal to Simon's Hⁿ), B_ρ(ξ) = closedBall ξ ρ (closed ball), ω_n = omega n ∈ (0, ∞), and Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ for every n-dimensional subspace P. For a rectifiable n-varifold V: μ = μ_V = V.weight; T_x = V.tangentSpace x; p_x and p_x^⊥ are the orthogonal projections onto T_x and T_x^⊥; div_M X(x) = V.tangentialDiv X x = trace(DX(x)∘p_x); ∇^M h(x) = V.tangentialGradient h x = p_x(∇h(x)); r = |x − ξ|; q_ξ(x) = V.normalRadialSq ξ x = |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|² ∈ [0, 1] (q_ξ(ξ) = 0 because division by 0 is 0); w_ξ(x) = q_ξ(x)/|x − ξ|ⁿ (w_ξ(ξ) = 0); a_ξ(ρ) = μ(B_ρ(ξ))/ρⁿ (a real number); Θ(ξ) = V.density ξ. A test field in U is a C¹ map X: E → E with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U (IsTestField). 'V has mean curvature H in U' (HasMeanCurvatureIn) means H ∈ L¹_loc(U, μ) and ∫div_M X dμ = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every test field X in U; 'stationary in U' means ∫div_M X dμ = 0 for every test field X in U. (FV) for V means: (FV1) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K; (FV2) dim T_x = n for μ-a.e. x; (FV3) x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. (GF) is the statement that (FV) holds for every n ≥ 1, every ℓ and every V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ (exactly the second conjunct of the sibling tangent_structure_first_variation); (AT) is the contract Prop ApproxTangentAE. Under (FV): q_ξ, w_ξ, ∇^M h (for h ∈ C¹(U), on U) and div_M X (for X ∈ C¹) are μ-a.e. strongly measurable, being continuous functions of p_x and of continuous data; |div_M X| ≤ (n+ℓ)‖DX‖ and div_M X = 0 off tsupport X, so div_M X is μ-integrable for every test field X; μ is a locally finite, hence outer regular, Borel measure, and μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0 (spt V = spt μ).

Source: Simon Ch. 4, 3.1–3.11. The identity 3.6 is the case h ≡ 1, H ≡ 0 of the sibling theorem weighted_monotonicity_identity (which contains the printed steps 3.2–3.5, with the corrected 3.5 prefactors); 3.8–3.11 then follow as printed.

Assume (GF). Fix n ≥ 1, ℓ, V, an open U with V stationary in U, and write μ = μ_V, a = a_ξ, w = w_ξ.

1. V has mean curvature 0 in U: the zero field is locally integrable, and ∫ div_M X dμ = 0 = −∫⟨X, 0⟩ dμ for every test field X in U.

2. (3.6) Let B_R(ξ) ⊆ U and 0 < σ ≤ ρ < R. Apply weighted_monotonicity_identity with H ≡ 0 and h ≡ 1 (C¹ on U, and tsupport h ∩ B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ B_R(ξ) ⊆ U), with (FV1)–(FV3) supplied by (GF). Since ∫_{B_τ}1 dμ = μ(B_τ), ∇^M 1 = p_x(∇1) = p_x(0) = 0 and 1·0 = 0, the τ-integral vanishes, and we get a(ρ) − a(σ) = ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} w dμ (that is, μ(B_ρ)/ρⁿ − μ(B_σ)/σⁿ = ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} q_ξ/|x − ξ|ⁿ dμ), with w μ-integrable on B_ρ ∖ B_σ. This is the first conjunct of StationaryMonotonicity.

3. (3.8) Since w ≥ 0, a is nondecreasing on (0, R): the MonotoneOn conjunct.

4. (3.9, 3.10) Let 0 < ρ < R. a ≥ 0 is nondecreasing on (0, ρ], so L := lim_{s↓0} a(s) = inf_{(0,ρ]} a exists and L ≥ 0. Then μ(B_s(ξ))/(ω_n sⁿ) = a(s)/ω_n → L/ω_n (ω_n > 0), i.e. V.HasDensityAt ξ (L/ω_n), and V.density ξ = L/ω_n (limUnder of a function converging along the non-trivial filter 𝓝[>]0). For s_k := ρ/(k + 1) the sets B_ρ ∖ B_{s_k} increase to B_ρ ∖ {ξ}; by monotone convergence and step 2, ∫_{B_ρ∖{ξ}} w dμ = lim_k (a(ρ) − a(s_k)) = a(ρ) − L < ∞. As w(ξ) = 0, w is μ-integrable on B_ρ (IntegrableOn) and ∫_{B_ρ} w dμ = a(ρ) − L; dividing by ω_n gives μ(B_ρ)/(ω_nρⁿ) − Θ(ξ) = ω_n^{-1}∫_{B_ρ} q_ξ/|x − ξ|ⁿ dμ. This completes StationaryMonotonicity.

5. (Existence of the density.) For ξ ∈ U there is R > 0 with B_R(ξ) ⊆ U (U open), and step 4 gives V.HasDensityAt ξ (V.density ξ). Moreover, by monotonicity, ω_nΘ(ξ) = inf_{(0,R)} a_ξ ≤ a_ξ(ρ) for all 0 < ρ < R.

6. (3.11, upper semicontinuity.) Let ξ ∈ U and t > Θ(ξ). Choose R > 0 with B_{2R}(ξ) ⊆ U, then ρ ∈ (0, R/2) with μ(B_ρ(ξ))/(ω_nρⁿ) < t (the quotient tends to Θ(ξ)), then δ ∈ (0, R/2) with μ(B_{ρ+δ}(ξ))/(ω_nρⁿ) < t (μ(B_{ρ+δ}(ξ)) ↓ μ(B_ρ(ξ)) as δ ↓ 0, since B_ρ(ξ) = ⋂_δ B_{ρ+δ}(ξ) and μ(B_{2R}(ξ)) < ∞). If |η − ξ| < δ, then B_R(η) ⊆ B_{2R}(ξ) ⊆ U and B_ρ(η) ⊆ B_{ρ+δ}(ξ), so step 5 at η (with radius R > ρ) gives Θ(η) ≤ μ(B_ρ(η))/(ω_nρⁿ) ≤ μ(B_{ρ+δ}(ξ))/(ω_nρⁿ) < t. Hence Θ is upper semicontinuous at every ξ ∈ U (within U), i.e. UpperSemicontinuousOn V.density U. With step 5 this is StationaryDensity.
proof_key_steps: Stationary means mean curvature 0
weighted_monotonicity_identity with h ≡ 1, H ≡ 0 gives 3.6 for 0 < σ ≤ ρ < R
w ≥ 0 gives monotonicity 3.8
Monotone limit gives existence of Θ(ξ) = lim a(s)/ω_n; monotone convergence gives integrability of w on B_ρ and 3.10
Θ(η) ≤ μ(B_ρ(η))/(ω_nρⁿ) ≤ μ(B_{ρ+δ}(ξ))/(ω_nρⁿ) for η near ξ gives upper semicontinuity 3.11

subproblems.title: Monotonicity with mean curvature: bounded (3.17), logarithmic error (3.18), Lᵖ (4.5–4.8) and Lᵖ density (4.9)
subproblems.statement: Assume (GF). Then: BoundedCurvatureMonotonicity (if V has mean curvature H in open U with |H| ≤ Λ μ_V-a.e. in U, Λ ≥ 0, then for every B_R(ξ) ⊆ U there are F with F(ρ) ∈ [e^{-Λρ}, e^{Λρ}] (0 < ρ < R) and G with G(σ,ρ) ∈ [e^{-ΛR}, e^{ΛR}] such that F(ρ)ρ^{-n}μ_V(B_ρ) − F(σ)σ^{-n}μ_V(B_σ) = G(σ,ρ)∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} q_ξ r^{-n}dμ_V for 0 < σ ≤ ρ < R, and Θ exists and is u.s.c. on U); LogarithmicMonotonicityError (3.18); LpMonotonicity (4.5, 4.7, 4.8 with κ = (p − n)/(4p), closed endpoint ρ = R); and LpDensity (4.9).

Source: Simon Ch. 4, 3.14–3.18 and 4.1–4.9, with the documented errata: with the sign convention 3.14(‡) the error term of 3.16/4.1 enters with a plus sign and the integrating factor is exp(−∫E); κ = (p − n)/(4p) in 4.2 (the printed p/(4(p − n)) does not give ∫_0^ρ|F_0| ≤ ½Λ(ρ/R)^{1−n/p}); the remark after 3.17 concerns U (not N ∩ U). The printed proofs apply an ε-dependent integrating factor before letting ε ↓ 0, which leaves F dependent on the cutoff. To obtain one F we take the limit ε ↓ 0 first — this is the sibling weighted_monotonicity_identity, i.e. 3.16/4.1 integrated from σ to ρ with ε ↓ 0 — and then apply the integrating factor to the integrated identity by the integration-by-parts Lemma of Step 2 (the product rule for the BV function ρ ↦ ρ^{-n}μ(B_ρ) and the absolutely continuous factor F). The bounds on F, E and G are the printed ones.

Assume (GF). Fix n ≥ 1, ℓ, V, an open U, H such that V has mean curvature H in U, and write μ = μ_V.

Step 1 (basic identity). Let B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U, ρ > 0, a := a_ξ, D(s, t) := ∫_{B_t∖B_s} w_ξ dμ ≥ 0 and e(τ) := τ^{-n-1}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩ dμ. For 0 < s ≤ t ≤ ρ:
(1.1) a(t) − a(s) = D(s, t) + ∫_{(s,t]} e(τ) dτ.
This is weighted_monotonicity_identity with h ≡ 1 (C¹; tsupport h ∩ B_t(ξ) ⊆ B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U), because ∫_{B_τ}1 dμ = μ(B_τ), ∇^M 1 = 0 and 1·H = H; its hypotheses (FV1)–(FV3) come from (GF). It also gives integrability of e on (s, t] and of w_ξ on B_t ∖ B_s. On [s, t], a and e are bounded Borel functions: τ ↦ μ(B_τ) is nondecreasing, τ ↦ ∫_{B_τ}⟨x − ξ, H⟩ dμ is the difference of the nondecreasing functions τ ↦ ∫_{B_τ} g⁺ dμ and τ ↦ ∫_{B_τ} g⁻ dμ with g := ⟨x − ξ, H⟩ ∈ L¹(μ⌞B_ρ), and |e(τ)| ≤ τ^{-n}∫_{B_ρ}|H| dμ.

Step 2 (integration by parts). Let 0 < σ ≤ ρ with (1.1) on [σ, ρ], and let F: [σ, ρ] → ℝ be absolutely continuous, F(t) = F(σ) + ∫_σ^t F'(τ) dτ with F' ∈ L¹(σ, ρ). Then
(2.1) F(ρ)a(ρ) − F(σ)a(σ) = ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} F(|x − ξ|) w_ξ(x) dμ(x) + ∫_σ^ρ (F(τ)e(τ) + F'(τ)a(τ)) dτ.
Proof: F(ρ)a(ρ) − F(σ)a(σ) = F(σ)(a(ρ) − a(σ)) + (F(ρ) − F(σ))a(ρ), and by (1.1) (F(ρ) − F(σ))a(ρ) = ∫_σ^ρ F'(t)[a(t) + D(t, ρ) + ∫_t^ρ e(s) ds] dt. As x ∈ B_ρ ∖ B_t iff t < |x − ξ| ≤ ρ, Fubini for the integrable function (t, x) ↦ F'(t)w_ξ(x)1_{t<|x−ξ|} on (σ, ρ] × (B_ρ ∖ B_σ) gives ∫_σ^ρ F'(t)D(t, ρ) dt = ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} w_ξ(x)(F(|x − ξ|) − F(σ)) dμ(x), and Fubini on {σ < t < s ≤ ρ} gives ∫_σ^ρ F'(t)∫_t^ρ e(s) ds dt = ∫_σ^ρ e(s)(F(s) − F(σ)) ds. Adding these to F(σ)(a(ρ) − a(σ)) = F(σ)D(σ, ρ) + F(σ)∫_σ^ρ e, the terms containing F(σ) cancel, which gives (2.1).

Step 3 (BoundedCurvatureMonotonicity, 3.16–3.17). Assume Λ ≥ 0 and |H| ≤ Λ μ-a.e. in U. Fix ξ, R with B_R(ξ) ⊆ U. If R ≤ 0, take F ≡ 1 and G ≡ 1 (all conditions are vacuous). Let R > 0; for τ ∈ (0, R), a and e are as in Step 1 (B_τ(ξ) ⊆ U). For μ-a.e. x ∈ B_τ(ξ), |⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩| ≤ τΛ, hence |e(τ)| ≤ Λa(τ). subproblems.title: Canonical representative (Simon 3.12–3.13) and the support representation 4.10(1)
subproblems.statement: Assume ApproxTangentAE and (GF). Then CanonicalRepresentative holds (for V stationary in open U: (M_V, Θ) with M_V = {x ∈ U : Θ(x) > 0} is an admissible pair with pairWeight n M_V Θ = μ_V⌞U; {x ∈ M_V : Θ(x) ≥ α} is relatively closed in U for α > 0; and if θ ≥ α > 0 μ_V-a.e. in U then M_V = spt V ∩ U and Θ ≥ α on M_V), and LpSupportRepresentation holds (for V with mean curvature H ∈ L^p_loc in open U, p > n, θ ≥ 1 μ_V-a.e. in U: Θ ≥ 1 on spt V ∩ U, (spt V ∩ U, Θ) is an admissible pair, and its weight is μ_V⌞U).
subproblems.lean_statement: ApproxTangentAE → (∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ), 0 < n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts V.weight ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, Module.finrank ℝ (V.tangentSpace x) = n) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection) V.weight) → CanonicalRepresentative ∧ LpSupportRepresentation
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions (used throughout). n ≥ 1 and ℓ ≥ 0 are integers, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, Hⁿ = μHE[n] (equal to Simon's Hⁿ), B_ρ(ξ) = closedBall ξ ρ (closed ball), ω_n = omega n ∈ (0, ∞), and Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ for every n-dimensional subspace P. For a rectifiable n-varifold V: μ = μ_V = V.weight; T_x = V.tangentSpace x; p_x and p_x^⊥ are the orthogonal projections onto T_x and T_x^⊥; div_M X(x) = V.tangentialDiv X x = trace(DX(x)∘p_x); ∇^M h(x) = V.tangentialGradient h x = p_x(∇h(x)); r = |x − ξ|; q_ξ(x) = V.normalRadialSq ξ x = |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|² ∈ [0, 1] (q_ξ(ξ) = 0 because division by 0 is 0); w_ξ(x) = q_ξ(x)/|x − ξ|ⁿ (w_ξ(ξ) = 0); a_ξ(ρ) = μ(B_ρ(ξ))/ρⁿ (a real number); Θ(ξ) = V.density ξ. A test field in U is a C¹ map X: E → E with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U (IsTestField). 'V has mean curvature H in U' (HasMeanCurvatureIn) means H ∈ L¹_loc(U, μ) and ∫div_M X dμ = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every test field X in U; 'stationary in U' means ∫div_M X dμ = 0 for every test field X in U. (FV) for V means: (FV1) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K; (FV2) dim T_x = n for μ-a.e. x; (FV3) x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. (GF) is the statement that (FV) holds for every n ≥ 1, every ℓ and every V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ (exactly the second conjunct of the sibling tangent_structure_first_variation); (AT) is the contract Prop ApproxTangentAE. Under (FV): q_ξ, w_ξ, ∇^M h (for h ∈ C¹(U), on U) and div_M X (for X ∈ C¹) are μ-a.e. strongly measurable, being continuous functions of p_x and of continuous data; |div_M X| ≤ (n+ℓ)‖DX‖ and div_M X = 0 off tsupport X, so div_M X is μ-integrable for every test field X; μ is a locally finite, hence outer regular, Borel measure, and μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0 (spt V = spt μ).

Source: Simon Ch. 4, 3.12–3.13 and 4.10(1): 'Since V = v(M, θ) and Θⁿ(V, x) = θ(x) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M (by Remark 1.8(2)), 3.11 enables us to choose canonical representatives M_V, θ_V …'. The equality Θ = θ Hⁿ-a.e. on M is the hypothesis ApproxTangentAE; the null set M_V ∖ M is handled with Ch. 1, Thm 3.3 (if Θ^{*n}(μ, A_2, x) ≥ t for all x ∈ A_1 ⊆ A_2 then t Hⁿ(A_1) ≤ μ(A_2)). The printed argument is expanded into a Lemma that uses only existence and upper semicontinuity of Θ on U, and is then applied with 3.9/3.11 (sibling stationary_monotonicity_density) and with 4.9 (sibling mean_curvature_monotonicity).

Assume (AT) and (GF).

Lemma. Let n ≥ 1, V a rectifiable n-varifold, μ = μ_V, U open, and suppose (a) V.HasDensityAt ξ (Θ(ξ)) for every ξ ∈ U and (b) Θ is upper semicontinuous on U. Let M_V := V.canonicalCarrier U = {x ∈ U : Θ(x) > 0}. Then (i) IsRectifiablePair n M_V Θ; (ii) pairWeight n M_V Θ = μ⌞U; (iii) for α > 0 there is a closed C with {x ∈ M_V : α ≤ Θ(x)} = C ∩ U; (iv) if α > 0 and V.MultiplicityGE α U, then M_V = spt V ∩ U and Θ ≥ α on M_V.
Proof of the Lemma.
1. Choose a pair a = (M, θ) with mk a = V; then μ = pairWeight n M θ. By (AT) for a, V.HasDensityAt x (θ x) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M; limits along 𝓝[>]0 are unique, so Θ(x) = θ(x) > 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M. (∗)
2. For α ∈ ℝ let S_α := {x ∈ U : α ≤ Θ(x)} and C_α := closure of S_α. Then S_α = C_α ∩ U: if x ∈ C_α ∩ U and t > Θ(x), by (b) there is a neighbourhood W of x with Θ < t on W ∩ U; W meets S_α ⊆ U, so α < t; as t > Θ(x) is arbitrary, α ≤ Θ(x). Consequently M_V = ⋃_{k≥1} (C_{1/k} ∩ U) is a Borel set, and the restriction of Θ to U is Borel measurable. For α > 0, {x ∈ M_V : α ≤ Θ(x)} = S_α = C_α ∩ U, which is (iii).
3. Hⁿ(M_V ∖ M) = 0. μ is concentrated on M (μ(E ∖ M) = 0 because μ = (Hⁿ⌞M) with density θ and M is Hⁿ-null-measurable), and μ is locally finite by (FV1), hence outer regular. Fix k, R ≥ 1 and A := {x ∈ U ∖ M : Θ(x) ≥ 1/k} ∩ B_R(0). Then A ⊆ E ∖ M, so A has outer μ-measure 0 and is contained in a Borel set B with μ(B) = 0 (a measurable hull); by outer regularity, for every δ > 0 there is an open O ⊇ B ⊇ A with μ(O) < δ. For x ∈ A the set O is a neighbourhood of x, so Θ^{*n}(μ, O, x) = limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(O ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) = Θ(x) ≥ 1/k by (a). Ch. 1, Thm 3.3 [SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_3] (A_1 = A, A_2 = O) gives (1/k)Hⁿ(A) ≤ μ(O) < δ; hence Hⁿ(A) = 0. Taking the union over k and R, Hⁿ(M_V ∖ M) = 0.
4. By (∗), Hⁿ((M ∩ U) ∖ M_V) = 0. Hence M_V and M ∩ U differ by an Hⁿ-null set, and Θ = θ Hⁿ-a.e. on M_V.
5. (i): M_V ⊆ M ∪ (M_V ∖ M), M is countably n-rectifiable and Hⁿ(M_V ∖ M) = 0; adding this null set to the exceptional set M_0 of Ch. 3, 1.1, M_V is countably n-rectifiable. M_V is Borel, hence Hⁿ-null-measurable. Θ > 0 on M_V by definition. For compact K, Θ is measurable on M_V ∩ K (step 2) and by step 4 ∫_{M_V∩K} Θ dHⁿ = ∫_{M_V∩K∩M} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞, so IntegrableOn Θ (M_V ∩ K) Hⁿ.
6. (ii): for Borel B, pairWeight n M_V Θ (B) = ∫_{B∩M_V} ofReal(Θ) dHⁿ = ∫_{B∩M∩U} θ dHⁿ = μ(B ∩ U) by step 4; measures agreeing on Borel sets are equal.
7. (iv): MultiplicityGE α U gives a pair b = (M', θ') with mk b = V and θ' ≥ α Hⁿ-a.e. on M' ∩ U. Step 1 applied to b gives Θ = θ' ≥ α Hⁿ-a.e. on M' ∩ U, and μ = pairWeight n M' θ' is absolutely continuous with respect to Hⁿ⌞M', so Θ ≥ α μ-a.e. on U. (α) spt V ∩ U ⊆ {Θ ≥ α}: if x ∈ spt V ∩ U had Θ(x) < α, by (b) there would be an open W ∋ x, W ⊆ U, with Θ < α on W; μ(W) > 0 since x ∈ spt μ, contradicting Θ ≥ α μ-a.e. on U. (β) M_V ⊆ spt V: if Θ(x) > 0 then μ(B_ρ(x)) > 0 for all small ρ > 0 (the quotients μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) tend to Θ(x) > 0) and hence for all ρ > 0, so every neighbourhood of x has positive measure. Therefore M_V ⊆ spt V ∩ U ⊆ {x ∈ U : Θ(x) ≥ α} ⊆ M_V (α > 0), so M_V = spt V ∩ U and Θ ≥ α on M_V. This proves the Lemma.

8. CanonicalRepresentative. Let n ≥ 1 and V stationary in the open U. The sibling stationary_monotonicity_density, applied with (GF), gives StationaryDensity: (a) and (b). The Lemma gives the four conjuncts (i)–(iv) of CanonicalRepresentative.

9. LpSupportRepresentation. Let n ≥ 1, V with mean curvature H in the open U, p > n, IsLocallyLp U H p, and MultiplicityGE 1 U. The sibling mean_curvature_monotonicity, applied with (GF), gives LpDensity: (a) and (b). By (iv) with α = 1, M_V = spt V ∩ U and 1 ≤ Θ(x) for every x ∈ spt V ∩ U. Substituting M_V = spt V ∩ U into (i) and (ii) gives IsRectifiablePair n (spt V ∩ U) Θ and pairWeight n (spt V ∩ U) Θ = μ⌞U.

Upper semicontinuity makes {Θ ≥ α} relatively closed in U, so M_V is Borel and Θ|U Borel

Hence (M_V, Θ) is an admissible pair with weight μ_V⌞U

Apply the Lemma with StationaryDensity (sibling) and with LpDensity (sibling, α = 1)

Documented corrections: the coefficient in 5.2 is Λ (not Λρ), which produces the factor e^{Λρ} of 5.4 (here via a Gronwall argument); only the full-ball case (σ = 0) of 4.10(2) is used — the annular version is false as printed. In the frozen statement the constants are quantified as ∀ α Γ, ∃ β c, so β and c may depend on n, α and Γ; we take β as in the printed proof and c := 8Γ/(α²ω_n), both fixed after n, α, Γ and before ℓ, V, U, H, Λ, h, ξ, ρ. (The defining inequality of β happens not to involve Γ; this extra observation is neither needed nor asserted by the frozen statement.)

Assume (AT) and (GF).

Choice of constants. Let n ≥ 1, α ∈ (0, 1) and Γ > 0 be given. Since (1 − α²)(1 − β')^{−n} → 1 − α² < 1 − α²/2 as β' ↓ 0, we may fix β ∈ (0, ½) with (1 − α²)(1 − β)^{−n} ≤ 1 − α²/2, and we put c := 8Γ/(α²ω_n) > 0. These β and c are the witnesses for ∃ β c in PoincareInequality (which comes after ∀ α Γ). Now let ℓ, V, U, H, Λ, h, ξ_0 := ξ and ρ satisfy the hypotheses, and write μ = μ_V.

1. Reductions. Replacing Λ by max(Λ, 0) preserves all hypotheses (|H| ≤ Λ ≤ max(Λ, 0), and e^{max(Λ,0)ρ} = max(e^{Λρ}, 1) ≤ 1 + α), so assume Λ ≥ 0. H is locally integrable on U and |H| ≤ Λ μ-a.e. on U, so H ∈ L^{n+1}(μ⌞K) for every compact K ⊆ U (bounded, strongly measurable, μ(K) < ∞): IsLocallyLp U H (n + 1) with n + 1 > n. By the siblings mean_curvature_monotonicity (LpDensity) and canonical_representatives (LpSupportRepresentation, with MultiplicityGE 1 U), both applied with (AT) and (GF): for every ζ ∈ U, μ(B_s(ζ))/(ω_n sⁿ) → Θ(ζ) as s ↓ 0, and Θ(ζ) ≥ 1 for every ζ ∈ spt μ ∩ U.

2. Gronwall form of 5.4. Let y ∈ E and r_1 > 0 with B_{r_1}(y) ⊆ U, and g ∈ C¹(U) with g ≥ 0 on U. Put f(s) := s^{−n}∫_{B_s(y)} g dμ for 0 < s ≤ r_1 and P := ∫_{(0,r_1]} τ^{−n−1}∫_{B_τ(y)} |x − y||∇^M g(x)| dμ(x) dτ ∈ [0, ∞]. Claim: f(s) ≤ e^{Λ(r_1−s)}(f(r_1) + P) for 0 < s ≤ r_1. Proof: by the sibling weighted_monotonicity_identity (function g, centre y, radii s' ≤ r_1; tsupport g ∩ B_{r_1}(y) ⊆ U), for s ≤ s' ≤ r_1, f(r_1) − f(s') = ∫_{B_{r_1}∖B_{s'}} g w_y dμ + ∫_{(s',r_1]} τ^{−n−1}∫_{B_τ(y)}⟨x − y, ∇^M g + gH⟩ dμ dτ. The first term is ≥ 0, and μ-a.e. on B_τ(y) ⊆ U, ⟨x − y, ∇^M g + gH⟩ ≥ −|x − y||∇^M g| − τΛg. Hence f(s') ≤ f(r_1) + P + Λ∫_{s'}^{r_1} f(τ) dτ for all s' ∈ [s, r_1], where f is bounded and Borel on [s, r_1]. If P = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise let C_0 := f(r_1) + P and u(s') := ∫_{s'}^{r_1} f; v(s') := e^{Λs'}u(s') is Lipschitz with v' = e^{Λs'}(Λu − f) ≥ −C_0e^{Λs'} a.e., so integrating from s' to r_1 gives Λu(s') ≤ C_0(e^{Λ(r_1−s')} − 1) (for Λ = 0 the claim is immediate), and f(s') ≤ C_0 + Λu(s') ≤ C_0e^{Λ(r_1−s')}. By Tonelli, P = ∫_{B_{r_1}(y)} |x − y||∇^M g(x)|∫_{(|x−y|,r_1]} τ^{−n−1} dτ dμ(x) ≤ (1/n)∫_{B_{r_1}(y)} |∇^M g(x)||x − y|^{1−n} dμ(x) (the point x = y contributes 0; here |x − y|^{1−n} ∈ [0, ∞]).
Growth bound: for y ∈ B_ρ(ξ_0), B_ρ(y) ⊆ B_{2ρ}(ξ_0) ⊆ U; with g ≡ 1 (∇^M g = 0, P = 0) and r_1 = ρ: μ(B_s(y)) ≤ e^{Λρ}(s/ρ)ⁿμ(B_ρ(y)) ≤ (1 + α)Γsⁿ ≤ 2Γsⁿ for 0 < s ≤ ρ; in particular μ({y}) = 0.
Kernel bound (4.10(2) for full balls, via 4.11): for y ∈ B_ρ(ξ_0) and 0 < s ≤ ρ, ∫_{B_s(y)} |x − y|^{1−n} dμ(x) ≤ 2nΓs. For n = 1 the integrand is 1 and this is the growth bound. For n ≥ 2 the layer-cake formula gives ∫_{B_s(y)}|x − y|^{1−n} dμ = ∫_0^∞ μ({x ∈ B_s(y) : |x − y|^{1−n} > λ}) dλ ≤ ∫_0^{s^{1−n}} μ(B_s(y)) dλ + ∫_{s^{1−n}}^∞ μ(B_{λ^{−1/(n−1)}}(y)) dλ ≤ 2Γs + 2Γ∫_{s^{1−n}}^∞ λ^{−n/(n−1)} dλ = 2Γs + 2Γ(n − 1)s.

3. Pointwise inequality (proof of 5.6, (1)–(2)). Fix ε > 0 and a C¹ nondecreasing ψ: ℝ → [0, 1] with ψ = 0 on (−∞, 0] and ψ = 1 on [ε, ∞). For t ≥ 0 let h_t := ψ(h − t) ∈ C¹(U): 0 ≤ h_t ≤ 1, h_t = 0 where h ≤ t, and ∇^M h_t = ψ'(h − t)∇^M h on U (chain rule; p_x is linear). Let r_0 := (1 − β)ρ and ζ ∈ B_{βρ}(ξ_0) ∩ spt μ with h(ζ) > t + ε; then B_{r_0}(ζ) ⊆ B_ρ(ξ_0) ⊆ U. Apply step 2 with g = h_t, y = ζ, r_1 = r_0 and let s ↓ 0: h_t is continuous at ζ and μ(B_s(ζ))/(ω_n sⁿ) → Θ(ζ) ≥ 1 (step 1), so s^{−n}∫_{B_s(ζ)} h_t dμ → ω_n h_t(ζ)Θ(ζ) ≥ ω_n h_t(ζ) = ω_n (h_t(ζ) = 1 because h(ζ) − t > ε). Using e^{Λr_0} ≤ e^{Λρ} ≤ 1 + α:
ω_n ≤ (1 + α)[r_0^{−n}∫_{B_{r_0}(ζ)} h_t dμ + (1/n)∫_{B_{r_0}(ζ)} ψ'(h − t)|∇^M h||x − ζ|^{1−n} dμ(x)].
Since h_t ≤ 1_{h>0} (t ≥ 0) and B_{r_0}(ζ) ⊆ B_ρ(ξ_0), r_0^{−n}∫_{B_{r_0}(ζ)} h_t dμ ≤ (1 − β)^{−n}ρ^{−n}μ({x ∈ B_ρ(ξ_0) : h(x) > 0}) ≤ (1 − β)^{−n}(1 − α)ω_n. Dividing by ω_n and using (1 + α)(1 − α)(1 − β)^{−n} ≤ 1 − α²/2 and 1 + α ≤ 2:
(3.1) α²/2 ≤ (2/(nω_n))∫_{B_ρ(ξ_0)} ψ'(h(x) − t)|∇^M h(x)||x − ζ|^{1−n}1_{|x−ζ|≤r_0} dμ(x).

4. Integration over ζ. Let A_t := {ζ ∈ B_{βρ}(ξ_0) : h(ζ) > t + ε}. μ-a.e. ζ ∈ A_t lies in spt μ (μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0), so integrating (3.1) over A_t with respect to μ and using Tonelli (nonnegative measurable integrands), (α²/2)μ(A_t) ≤ (2/(nω_n))∫_{B_ρ(ξ_0)} ψ'(h(x) − t)|∇^M h(x)|[∫_{B_{r_0}(x)} |x − ζ|^{1−n} dμ(ζ)] dμ(x) ≤ (4Γρ/ω_n)∫_{B_ρ(ξ_0)} ψ'(h − t)|∇^M h| dμ, by the kernel bound of step 2 (x ∈ B_ρ(ξ_0), r_0 ≤ ρ).

5. Integration over t (4.11). By the layer-cake formula (Mathlib MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt) ∫_0^∞ μ(A_t) dt = ∫_{B_{βρ}(ξ_0)} (h − ε)^+ dμ, and ∫_0^∞ ψ'(h(x) − t) dt = ψ(h(x)) ≤ 1 for x ∈ U (h(x) ≥ 0). By Tonelli, ∫_{B_{βρ}(ξ_0)} (h − ε)^+ dμ ≤ (8Γ/(α²ω_n))ρ∫_{B_ρ(ξ_0)} |∇^M h| dμ. Letting ε ↓ 0 (monotone convergence; h ≥ 0 on B_{βρ}(ξ_0) ⊆ U) gives ∫_{B_{βρ}(ξ_0)} h dμ ≤ cρ∫_{B_ρ(ξ_0)} |∇^M h| dμ, which is PoincareInequality with the constants β, c chosen above (0 < β < ½, c > 0).
proof_key_steps: Given n, α, Γ (frozen order ∀ α Γ ∃ β c), fix β ∈ (0, ½) with (1−α²)(1−β)^{−n} ≤ 1 − α²/2 and c = 8Γ/(α²ω_n), before ℓ and all data
Bounded H is L^{n+1}_loc, so LpDensity and LpSupportRepresentation give existence of Θ on U and Θ ≥ 1 on spt V ∩ U
weighted_monotonicity_identity plus Gronwall gives 5.4: f(s) ≤ e^{Λ(r_1−s)}(f(r_1) + (1/n)∫|∇^M g||x−y|^{1−n})
Growth μ(B_s(y)) ≤ 2Γsⁿ and the full-ball kernel bound ∫_{B_s(y)}|x−y|^{1−n} ≤ 2nΓs
Apply 5.4 to the truncations ψ(h − t) at ζ ∈ B_{βρ} ∩ spt V with h(ζ) > t + ε to get α²/2 ≤ (2/(nω_n))∫ψ'(h−t)|∇^M h||x−ζ|^{1−n}
Integrate over ζ (Tonelli + kernel bound) and over t (layer cake), then let ε ↓ 0

subproblems.title: Michael–Simon Sobolev inequality (Simon 5.7–5.9, corrected Lemma 5.8, n ≥ 2)
subproblems.statement: Assume ApproxTangentAE and (GF). Then SobolevInequality holds: for n ≥ 2 there is c = c(n) > 0 (one may take c = 5^{n+1}ω_n^{−1/n}), independent of ℓ, such that if V has generalized mean curvature H (merely L¹_loc) in an open U, θ ≥ 1 μ_V-a.e. in U, and h ∈ C¹(U) is nonnegative with compact support in U, then (∫ h^{n/(n−1)} dμ_V)^{(n−1)/n} ≤ c∫(|∇^M h| + h|H|) dμ_V.
subproblems.lean_statement: ApproxTangentAE → (∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ), 0 < n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts V.weight ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, Module.finrank ℝ (V.tangentSpace x) = n) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection) V.weight) → SobolevInequality
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions (used throughout). n ≥ 1 and ℓ ≥ 0 are integers, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, Hⁿ = μHE[n] (equal to Simon's Hⁿ), B_ρ(ξ) = closedBall ξ ρ (closed ball), ω_n = omega n ∈ (0, ∞), and Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ for every n-dimensional subspace P. For a rectifiable n-varifold V: μ = μ_V = V.weight; T_x = V.tangentSpace x; p_x and p_x^⊥ are the orthogonal projections onto T_x and T_x^⊥; div_M X(x) = V.tangentialDiv X x = trace(DX(x)∘p_x); ∇^M h(x) = V.tangentialGradient h x = p_x(∇h(x)); r = |x − ξ|; q_ξ(x) = V.normalRadialSq ξ x = |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|² ∈ [0, 1] (q_ξ(ξ) = 0 because division by 0 is 0); w_ξ(x) = q_ξ(x)/|x − ξ|ⁿ (w_ξ(ξ) = 0); a_ξ(ρ) = μ(B_ρ(ξ))/ρⁿ (a real number); Θ(ξ) = V.density ξ. A test field in U is a C¹ map X: E → E with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U (IsTestField). 'V has mean curvature H in U' (HasMeanCurvatureIn) means H ∈ L¹_loc(U, μ) and ∫div_M X dμ = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every test field X in U; 'stationary in U' means ∫div_M X dμ = 0 for every test field X in U. (FV) for V means: (FV1) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K; (FV2) dim T_x = n for μ-a.e. x; (FV3) x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. (GF) is the statement that (FV) holds for every n ≥ 1, every ℓ and every V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ (exactly the second conjunct of the sibling tangent_structure_first_variation); (AT) is the contract Prop ApproxTangentAE. Under (FV): q_ξ, w_ξ, ∇^M h (for h ∈ C¹(U), on U) and div_M X (for X ∈ C¹) are μ-a.e. strongly measurable, being continuous functions of p_x and of continuous data; |div_M X| ≤ (n+ℓ)‖DX‖ and div_M X = 0 off tsupport X, so div_M X is μ-integrable for every test field X; μ is a locally finite, hence outer regular, Borel measure, and μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0 (spt V = spt μ).

Source: Simon Ch. 4, 5.5, 5.7, 5.8, 5.9 (with 4.11 and the 5-times covering Lemma 3.4 of Ch. 1). Documented corrections: 5.7 requires n ≥ 2, and 'c does not depend on k' means ℓ; Lemma 5.8 is inconsistent as printed (its lower bound 1 ≤ σ^{−n}f(σ) for all σ contradicts boundedness of f) and is replaced by the corrected Lemma of Step 2 (lower bound only along small radii, finite-interval inequality, same conclusion); as in 5.9 only H ∈ L¹_loc is used, and Θ ≥ 1 is used only μ-a.e. (where Θ = θ, by ApproxTangentAE). The constant is c = 5^{n+1}ω_n^{−1/n}.

Assume (AT) and (GF). Fix n ≥ 2, c := 5^{n+1}ω_n^{−1/n} > 0, and let ℓ, V, U, H, h be as in SobolevInequality; μ = μ_V.

1. Preliminaries. h is C¹ on E (C¹ on U, and identically 0 on the open set E ∖ tsupport h, which together with U covers E). K_h := tsupport h is compact and ⊆ U; h and ∇^M h are bounded, μ-a.e. strongly measurable by (GF), and vanish off K_h; H ∈ L¹(μ⌞K_h); so all integrals below are finite. MultiplicityGE 1 U gives a pair b = (M', θ') with mk b = V and θ' ≥ 1 Hⁿ-a.e. on M' ∩ U; by (AT) for b, μ(B_s(ζ))/(ω_n sⁿ) → θ'(ζ) for Hⁿ-a.e. ζ ∈ M'; since μ is absolutely continuous with respect to Hⁿ⌞M':
(1.1) for μ-a.e. ζ ∈ U, Θ(ζ) exists (HasDensityAt) and Θ(ζ) ≥ 1.
For g ∈ C¹(U) with g ≥ 0 and tsupport g ⊆ K_h, and ζ ∈ E, put f_ζ(τ) := ω_n^{−1}∫_{B_τ(ζ)} g dμ and k_ζ(τ) := ω_n^{−1}∫_{B_τ(ζ)} (|∇^M g| + g|H|) dμ (τ > 0): both are nondecreasing and bounded, and sup f_ζ = ω_n^{−1}∫ g dμ (attained for τ large).
(5.5) For 0 < s ≤ r: s^{−n}f_ζ(s) ≤ r^{−n}f_ζ(r) + ∫_s^r τ^{−n}k_ζ(τ) dτ. Indeed the sibling weighted_monotonicity_identity applies for every radius r because tsupport g ∩ B_r(ζ) ⊆ K_h ⊆ U; its annulus term is ≥ 0, and |⟨x − ζ, ∇^M g + gH⟩| ≤ τ(|∇^M g| + g|H|) on B_τ(ζ).

2. Corrected Lemma 5.8. Let n ≥ 2 and f, k: (0, ∞) → [0, ∞) be nondecreasing with f bounded, f_∞ := sup f, such that (a) s^{−n}f(s) ≤ r^{−n}f(r) + ∫_s^r τ^{−n}k(τ) dτ for 0 < s ≤ r, and (b) limsup_{s↓0} s^{−n}f(s) ≥ 1. Then f_∞ > 0 and, with r_0 := 2f_∞^{1/n}, there is r ∈ (0, r_0) with f(5r) ≤ ½·5ⁿ r_0 k(r).
Proof: f_∞ > 0 by (b). Suppose k(r) < 2·5^{−n}r_0^{−1}f(5r) for all r ∈ (0, r_0). Fix s ∈ (0, r_0) and let S := sup_{τ∈[s,r_0]} τ^{−n}f(τ) ≤ s^{−n}f_∞ < ∞. For s' ∈ [s, r_0], (a) with r = r_0 and the substitution u = 5τ give s'^{−n}f(s') ≤ r_0^{−n}f_∞ + (2/(5ⁿr_0))∫_{s'}^{r_0} τ^{−n}f(5τ) dτ = r_0^{−n}f_∞ + (2/(5r_0))∫_{5s'}^{5r_0} u^{−n}f(u) du ≤ r_0^{−n}f_∞ + (2/(5r_0))[r_0 S + f_∞ r_0^{1−n}/(n − 1)], because [5s', 5r_0] ⊆ [s, r_0] ∪ [r_0, ∞) and ∫_{r_0}^∞ u^{−n} du = r_0^{1−n}/(n − 1). As n ≥ 2 and r_0^{−n}f_∞ = 2^{−n}, taking the supremum over s' gives S ≤ (7/5)2^{−n} + (2/5)S, so S ≤ (7/3)2^{−n} ≤ 7/12. Thus s^{−n}f(s) ≤ 7/12 for every s ∈ (0, r_0), contradicting (b).

3. Good balls (proof of 5.7, (1)). Let g be as in step 1 and G_g := {ζ ∈ U : g(ζ) ≥ 1, Θ(ζ) exists and Θ(ζ) ≥ 1}. For ζ ∈ G_g, s^{−n}f_ζ(s) = (ω_n sⁿ)^{−1}∫_{B_s(ζ)} g dμ → g(ζ)Θ(ζ) ≥ 1 (g is continuous at ζ). By step 2 with f = f_ζ, k = k_ζ there is r_ζ ∈ (0, r_0), r_0 := 2(ω_n^{−1}∫ g dμ)^{1/n}, with
∫_{B_{5r_ζ}(ζ)} g dμ ≤ 5ⁿ ω_n^{−1/n}(∫ g dμ)^{1/n}∫_{B_{r_ζ}(ζ)} (|∇^M g| + g|H|) dμ.

4. Covering. {g ≥ 1} ⊆ K_h ⊆ U, so by (1.1) μ({g ≥ 1} ∖ G_g) = 0. The closed balls B_{r_ζ}(ζ), ζ ∈ G_g, have radii < r_0; by the 5-times covering Lemma (Ch. 1, 3.4; Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall) there is a pairwise disjoint subfamily {B_{r_j}(ζ_j)} — countable, since disjoint balls with nonempty interior in E are countably many — with G_g ⊆ ⋃_j B_{5r_j}(ζ_j). Summing step 3 over j (g ≥ 0, the small balls are disjoint):
(4.1) ∫_{{g ≥ 1}} g dμ ≤ 5ⁿ ω_n^{−1/n}(∫ g dμ)^{1/n}∫ (|∇^M g| + g|H|) dμ.

5. Truncation and layer cake (end of the proof of 5.7). Fix ε ∈ (0, 1] and ψ ∈ C¹(ℝ) nondecreasing with 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1, ψ = 0 on (−∞, 0] and ψ = 1 on [ε, ∞). For t ≥ 0 let h_t := ψ(h − t) (C¹ on U, ≥ 0, tsupport h_t ⊆ K_h) and M_s := {h > s}. Then {h_t ≥ 1} ⊇ M_{t+ε}, h_t ≤ 1_{M_t} and |∇^M h_t| = ψ'(h − t)|∇^M h|. Applying (4.1) to g = h_t:
μ(M_{t+ε}) ≤ 5ⁿ ω_n^{−1/n} μ(M_t)^{1/n}[∫ ψ'(h − t)|∇^M h| dμ + ∫_{M_t} |H| dμ].
Since (t + ε)^{n/(n−1)}μ(M_t) ≤ ∫_{M_t} (h + ε)^{n/(n−1)} dμ ≤ Q_ε := ∫_{M_0} (h + ε)^{n/(n−1)} dμ, multiplying by (t + ε)^{1/(n−1)} gives
(t + ε)^{1/(n−1)}μ(M_{t+ε}) ≤ 5ⁿ ω_n^{−1/n} Q_ε^{1/n}[∫ ψ'(h − t)|∇^M h| dμ + ∫_{M_t} |H| dμ].
Integrate over t ∈ (0, ∞) (Tonelli; 4.11): the left side equals ∫_ε^∞ u^{1/(n−1)}μ(M_u) du = ((n − 1)/n)∫_{M_ε} (h^{n/(n−1)} − ε^{n/(n−1)}) dμ; on the right, ∫_0^∞ ψ'(h(x) − t) dt = ψ(h(x)) ≤ 1 and ∫_0^∞ 1_{M_t}(x) dt = h(x). Hence ((n − 1)/n)∫_{M_ε}(h^{n/(n−1)} − ε^{n/(n−1)}) dμ ≤ 5ⁿ ω_n^{−1/n} Q_ε^{1/n}∫ (|∇^M h| + h|H|) dμ.

6. Let ε ↓ 0: by dominated convergence (integrands bounded on the compact K_h, μ(K_h) < ∞) the left side tends to ((n − 1)/n)Q with Q := ∫ h^{n/(n−1)} dμ, and Q_ε → Q. If Q = 0, the asserted inequality reads 0 ≤ c∫(|∇^M h| + h|H|) dμ, which holds as the integrand is ≥ 0. If Q > 0, dividing by Q^{1/n} gives Q^{(n−1)/n} ≤ (n/(n − 1))5ⁿ ω_n^{−1/n}∫(|∇^M h| + h|H|) dμ ≤ c∫(|∇^M h| + h|H|) dμ, since n/(n − 1) ≤ 2 ≤ 5. The constant c depends only on n, which proves SobolevInequality.
proof_key_steps: h is C¹ with compact support in U; ApproxTangentAE and MultiplicityGE give Θ ≥ 1 μ-a.e. in U
weighted_monotonicity_identity gives 5.5 for all radii: s^{−n}f(s) ≤ r^{−n}f(r) + ∫_s^r τ^{−n}k(τ)dτ
Corrected Lemma 5.8 (n ≥ 2, lower bound only as s ↓ 0) yields a good radius r < 2f_∞^{1/n} with f(5r) ≤ ½5ⁿ r_0 k(r)
5-times covering of the good balls gives ∫_{g≥1} g ≤ 5ⁿω_n^{−1/n}(∫g)^{1/n}∫(|∇^M g| + g|H|)
Apply to truncations ψ(h − t), multiply by (t+ε)^{1/(n−1)}, integrate in t (layer cake), let ε ↓ 0 and divide by Q^{1/n}

subproblems.title: Support in a ball and the convex hull property (Simon 6.1–6.2)
subproblems.statement: Assume (GF). Then SupportInBall holds (if n ≥ 1, R ≥ 0, V has L¹_loc generalized mean curvature H in U = ℝ^{n+ℓ} ∖ B_R(ξ) with n^{-1}|H(x)·(x − ξ)| < 1 for μ_V-a.e. x ∈ U, and spt V is compact, then spt V ⊆ B_R(ξ)), and ConvexHullProperty holds (if n ≥ 1, K is compact, spt V is compact and V is stationary in ℝ^{n+ℓ} ∖ K, then spt V ⊆ conv K).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ), 0 < n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts V.weight ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, Module.finrank ℝ (V.tangentSpace x) = n) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection) V.weight) → SupportInBall ∧ ConvexHullProperty
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions (used throughout). n ≥ 1 and ℓ ≥ 0 are integers, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, Hⁿ = μHE[n] (equal to Simon's Hⁿ), B_ρ(ξ) = closedBall ξ ρ (closed ball), ω_n = omega n ∈ (0, ∞), and Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ for every n-dimensional subspace P. For a rectifiable n-varifold V: μ = μ_V = V.weight; T_x = V.tangentSpace x; p_x and p_x^⊥ are the orthogonal projections onto T_x and T_x^⊥; div_M X(x) = V.tangentialDiv X x = trace(DX(x)∘p_x); ∇^M h(x) = V.tangentialGradient h x = p_x(∇h(x)); r = |x − ξ|; q_ξ(x) = V.normalRadialSq ξ x = |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|² ∈ [0, 1] (q_ξ(ξ) = 0 because division by 0 is 0); w_ξ(x) = q_ξ(x)/|x − ξ|ⁿ (w_ξ(ξ) = 0); a_ξ(ρ) = μ(B_ρ(ξ))/ρⁿ (a real number); Θ(ξ) = V.density ξ. A test field in U is a C¹ map X: E → E with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U (IsTestField). 'V has mean curvature H in U' (HasMeanCurvatureIn) means H ∈ L¹_loc(U, μ) and ∫div_M X dμ = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every test field X in U; 'stationary in U' means ∫div_M X dμ = 0 for every test field X in U. (FV) for V means: (FV1) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K; (FV2) dim T_x = n for μ-a.e. x; (FV3) x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. (GF) is the statement that (FV) holds for every n ≥ 1, every ℓ and every V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ (exactly the second conjunct of the sibling tangent_structure_first_variation); (AT) is the contract Prop ApproxTangentAE. Under (FV): q_ξ, w_ξ, ∇^M h (for h ∈ C¹(U), on U) and div_M X (for X ∈ C¹) are μ-a.e. strongly measurable, being continuous functions of p_x and of continuous data; |div_M X| ≤ (n+ℓ)‖DX‖ and div_M X = 0 off tsupport X, so div_M X is μ-integrable for every test field X; μ is a locally finite, hence outer regular, Borel measure, and μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0 (spt V = spt μ).

Source: Simon Ch. 4, 6.1 and 6.2. In 6.1 the printed identity is the first variation identity of the sibling radial_first_variation, applied to X(x) = ζ(x)γ(|x − ξ|)(x − ξ) with ζ ≡ 1 near spt V and γ ≥ 0 nondecreasing, γ = 0 on (−∞, R + ε]; with the sign convention 3.14(‡) its right side is −∫ γ(r)⟨x − ξ, H⟩ dμ (only |⟨x − ξ, H⟩| is used, so the printed sign is immaterial). 6.2 is reduced to 6.1 through the description of conv K by balls, which we prove.

Assume (GF).

SupportInBall.
1. Let n ≥ 1, R ≥ 0, U := E ∖ B_R(ξ) (open), V with mean curvature H in U, |⟨H(x), x − ξ⟩| < n for μ-a.e. x ∈ U, and spt V compact; μ = μ_V. Fix ε > 0.
2. Test field. Let W be the open 1-neighbourhood of spt V (bounded) and choose ζ ∈ C^∞_c(E) with 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 and ζ = 1 on W. Let γ(t) := (max(t − R − ε, 0))²: γ ∈ C¹(ℝ), γ ≥ 0, γ'(t) = 2 max(t − R − ε, 0) ≥ 0, γ(t) = 0 for t ≤ R + ε and γ(t) > 0 for t > R + ε. The field X(x) := (ζ(x)γ(|x − ξ|))(x − ξ) is C¹ (γ(|x − ξ|) vanishes on ball ξ (R + ε), a neighbourhood of ξ, and is C¹ away from ξ), has compact support (inside tsupport ζ), and tsupport X ⊆ {x : |x − ξ| ≥ R + ε} ⊆ U. So X is a test field in U, and ζ ∈ C¹(U).
3. By (GF), dim T_x = n for μ-a.e. x. The sibling radial_first_variation (with h := ζ and this γ) gives
∫_U [ζ(nγ(r) + rγ'(r)(1 − q_ξ)) + γ(r)⟨x − ξ, ∇^Mζ⟩] dμ = −∫_U ζγ(r)⟨x − ξ, H⟩ dμ.
4. μ(E ∖ spt V) = 0, and on the open set W ⊇ spt V we have ζ = 1 and ∇ζ = 0, hence ∇^Mζ = 0. So μ-a.e. the integrands equal nγ(r) + rγ'(r)(1 − q_ξ) and γ(r)⟨x − ξ, H⟩. These functions are μ-integrable on U: μ-a.e. on U they vanish off the compact set spt V ∩ {|x − ξ| ≥ R + ε} ⊆ U, on which γ(r) and rγ'(r) are bounded, q_ξ ∈ [0, 1] is μ-measurable by (GF), and H is μ-integrable (H ∈ L¹_loc(U, μ)). Therefore
n∫_U γ(r) dμ + ∫_U rγ'(r)(1 − q_ξ) dμ = −∫_U γ(r)⟨x − ξ, H⟩ dμ ≤ ∫_U γ(r)|⟨x − ξ, H⟩| dμ.
5. As rγ'(r)(1 − q_ξ) ≥ 0, ∫_U γ(r)(n − |⟨H, x − ξ⟩|) dμ ≤ 0. The integrand is ≥ 0 μ-a.e. on U (γ ≥ 0, and n − |⟨H, x − ξ⟩| > 0 μ-a.e. on U), so it vanishes μ-a.e. on U, whence γ(r) = 0 μ-a.e. on U. Since γ(r) > 0 on the open set O_ε := {x : |x − ξ| > R + ε} ⊆ U, μ(O_ε) = 0, so O_ε ∩ spt V = ∅, i.e. spt V ⊆ B_{R+ε}(ξ).
6. Since ε > 0 is arbitrary and ⋂_{ε>0} B_{R+ε}(ξ) = B_R(ξ), spt V ⊆ B_R(ξ).

ConvexHullProperty.
7. Let n ≥ 1, K compact, spt V compact, V stationary in E ∖ K, and y ∉ conv K. It suffices to find c ∈ E and R' ≥ 0 with K ⊆ B_{R'}(c) and y ∉ B_{R'}(c). Indeed, then E ∖ B_{R'}(c) ⊆ E ∖ K, so every test field in E ∖ B_{R'}(c) is a test field in E ∖ K and V has mean curvature 0 in E ∖ B_{R'}(c) (the zero field is locally integrable, and ∫ div_M X dμ = 0 = −∫⟨X, 0⟩ dμ); the hypothesis n^{-1}|⟨0, x − c⟩| = 0 < 1 holds everywhere; so SupportInBall gives spt V ⊆ B_{R'}(c), which does not contain y. As y ∉ conv K was arbitrary, spt V ⊆ conv K.
8. If K = ∅, take any c ≠ y (E has dimension n + ℓ ≥ 1) and R' = 0. If K ≠ ∅: conv K is convex and compact: by Carathéodory's theorem (Mathlib eq_pos_convex_span_of_mem_convexHull) every point of conv K is a convex combination of at most N + 1 points of K, N := n + ℓ, so conv K is the image of the compact set Δ_N × K^{N+1} (Δ_N the standard simplex of weights) under the continuous map (λ, x_0, …, x_N) ↦ Σ_i λ_i x_i, every such combination lying in conv K. By the separation theorem for the closed convex set conv K and the point y ∉ conv K (Mathlib geometric_hahn_banach_point_closed, with the Riesz representation of the separating functional) there are a unit vector e and m ∈ ℝ with ⟨e, x⟩ ≤ m for all x ∈ conv K and ⟨e, y⟩ = m + η with η > 0. Let z := y − ηe (so ⟨e, z⟩ = m), D := max_{x∈K} |x − z|, and for L > 0 let c_L := z − Le and R_L := (L² + D²)^{1/2}. For x ∈ K, |x − c_L|² = |x − z|² + 2L⟨e, x − z⟩ + L² ≤ D² + L², because ⟨e, x − z⟩ = ⟨e, x⟩ − m ≤ 0; so K ⊆ B_{R_L}(c_L). And |y − c_L|² = |ηe + Le|² = η² + 2Lη + L² > L² + D² as soon as L > D²/(2η); so y ∉ B_{R_L}(c_L). This proves ConvexHullProperty.

Source: Simon Ch. 4, 6.3, with the erratum dist(y, T_xV) → dist(y − x, T_xV). The uniform lower density bound (1) of the printed proof follows from 4.7 with σ ↓ 0 (sibling mean_curvature_monotonicity: LpMonotonicity, LpDensity) and 4.10(1) (sibling canonical_representatives: LpSupportRepresentation); (2) and the conclusion are as printed. Only the convergence of the blow-ups is used, for whatever multiplicity c > 0 appears in IsApproxTangentAt.

Assume (AT) and (GF). Let n ≥ 1, U open, V with mean curvature H in U, MultiplicityGE 1 U, p > n, IsLocallyLp U H p, x ∈ U, and V.IsApproxTangentAt x P with constant c > 0 (so dim P = n). Write μ = μ_V, κ := lpKappa n p > 0, and d(y) := infDist(y − x, P); d is 1-Lipschitz and d(y) ≤ |y − x| since 0 ∈ P.

1. Uniform lower density (printed (1)). Choose R > 0 with B_{2R}(x) ⊆ U, put A_0 := (R^{p−n}∫_{B_{2R}(x)} |H|^p dμ)^{1/p} < ∞ and Λ := A_0/κ ≥ 0. For ζ ∈ B_R(x): B_R(ζ) ⊆ B_{2R}(x) ⊆ U and (R^{p−n}∫_{B_R(ζ)} |H|^p dμ)^{1/p} ≤ A_0 = κΛ, so LpMonotonicity at the centre ζ with radius R gives F_ζ with 0 < e^{−(Λ/2)t(s)} ≤ F_ζ(s) ≤ e^{(Λ/2)t(s)} and |F_ζ(s) − 1| ≤ C_Λ t(s) for s ∈ (0, R], where t(s) := (s/R)^{1−n/p} ∈ (0, 1] and C_Λ := (e^{Λ/2}/2)Λ, and with Ψ_ζ(s) := F_ζ(s)a_ζ(s) + F_ζ(s) − 1 nondecreasing on (0, R]. If moreover ζ ∈ spt V, then by LpDensity Θ(ζ) exists and by LpSupportRepresentation Θ(ζ) ≥ 1, so a_ζ(s) → ω_nΘ(ζ) ≥ ω_n and, since F_ζ(s) → 1, Ψ_ζ(s) → ω_nΘ(ζ) ≥ ω_n as s ↓ 0; by monotonicity Ψ_ζ(s) ≥ ω_n for every s ∈ (0, R], i.e. F_ζ(s)a_ζ(s) ≥ ω_n − (F_ζ(s) − 1) ≥ ω_n − C_Λ t(s). Now fix t_0 ∈ (0, 1] so small that C_Λ t_0 ≤ ω_n/4 and e^{(Λ/2)t_0} ≤ 3/2 (both inequalities hold for all sufficiently small t_0 > 0), and put ρ_0 := R·t_0^{p/(p−n)} ∈ (0, R]. Since s ↦ t(s) is increasing with t(ρ_0) = t_0, we have t(s) ≤ t_0 for 0 < s ≤ ρ_0. Hence, for ζ ∈ spt V ∩ B_R(x) and 0 < s ≤ ρ_0: F_ζ(s)a_ζ(s) ≥ ω_n − C_Λ t_0 ≥ (3/4)ω_n and 0 < F_ζ(s) ≤ e^{(Λ/2)t_0} ≤ 3/2, so a_ζ(s) ≥ ((3/4)ω_n)/(3/2) = ω_n/2. No monotonicity in s of any lower bound is used; ρ_0 is chosen directly through t_0. Thus
(1) μ(B_s(ζ)) ≥ (ω_n/2)sⁿ for all ζ ∈ spt V ∩ B_R(x) and 0 < s ≤ ρ_0.

2. (Printed (2).) Let 0 < ρ ≤ ρ_0, ε > 0, α ∈ (0, ½), and suppose μ(B_ρ(x) ∖ {y : d(y) < ερ}) < (ω_n/2)αⁿρⁿ. Then d(ζ) < (ε + α)ρ for every ζ ∈ spt V ∩ B_{ρ/2}(x). Indeed, if d(ζ) ≥ (ε + α)ρ, then every y ∈ B_{αρ}(ζ) satisfies |y − x| ≤ αρ + ρ/2 < ρ and d(y) ≥ d(ζ) − |y − ζ| ≥ ερ, so B_{αρ}(ζ) ⊆ B_ρ(x) ∖ {d < ερ} and μ(B_{αρ}(ζ)) < (ω_n/2)(αρ)ⁿ; but ζ ∈ spt V ∩ B_R(x) (ρ/2 ≤ R) and αρ ≤ ρ_0, contradicting (1).

3. Blow-up. For every ε > 0, ρ^{−n}μ(B_ρ(x) ∖ {d < ερ}) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. Let f(z) := min(1, max(0, 2 − |z|))·min(1, max(0, 2 infDist(z, P)/ε − 1)). Then f ∈ C_c(E), 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, f = 0 on P (so ∫_P f dHⁿ = 0), and f(z) = 1 when |z| ≤ 1 and infDist(z, P) ≥ ε. Since P is a linear subspace, infDist(ρ^{−1}(y − x), P) = ρ^{−1}d(y), so the indicator of B_ρ(x) ∖ {d < ερ} at y is ≤ f(ρ^{−1}(y − x)), and ρ^{−n}μ(B_ρ(x) ∖ {d < ερ}) ≤ ρ^{−n}∫ f(ρ^{−1}(y − x)) dμ(y) → c∫_P f dHⁿ = 0 by IsApproxTangentAt.

4. Conclusion. Let S(ρ) := sSup{ρ^{−1}d(y) : y ∈ spt V ∩ B_ρ(x)}. This set of reals is bounded above by 1 and consists of nonnegative numbers, so S(ρ) ≥ 0 (also when it is empty, since sSup ∅ = 0). Given η > 0 put ε := η/8 and α := min(η/8, 1/4). By step 3 there is ρ_1 > 0 with μ(B_ρ(x) ∖ {d < ερ}) < (ω_n/2)αⁿρⁿ for 0 < ρ < ρ_1. For 0 < ρ' < min(ρ_0, ρ_1)/2, step 2 with ρ := 2ρ' gives ρ'^{−1}d(y) < 2(ε + α) ≤ η/2 for all y ∈ spt V ∩ B_{ρ'}(x), so 0 ≤ S(ρ') ≤ η/2 < η. Hence S(ρ') → 0 as ρ' ↓ 0, which is ClassicalTangent.
